rules.easyFirst: Do not start deep capability work while meaningful easy user-facing items remain.
rules.provenLive: PROVEN_LIVE requires the real user-facing workflow to pass. Code existing and tests passing is NOT proof.
rules.acceptanceGate: The gate is the app's own test command + tsc -b + live browser acceptance. A pre-commit hook is not the acceptance suite.
rules.costDiscipline: owned -> open-source -> self-hosted -> free tier -> partner credits -> paid. No recurring paid dependency enters quietly.
rules.honestUnavailable: A capability that is not ready must refuse truthfully rather than appear to work.
rules.productionTruthIsPostgres: PostgreSQL is production truth. SQLite is LEGACY / REFERENCE-ONLY: useful as historical implementation evidence, never qualified, deployed, or designed around. Any adapter-parity comparison is INFORMATIONAL ONLY unless the PostgreSQL implementation is independently proven. Owner ruling 2026-08-27, prompted by the carry-forward defect — "SQLite already does it correctly" explained the bug but proved nothing about the fix.
rules.noSilentSqliteFallback: 🚨 SQLite is NOT an accepted MigraPilot/MigraAI persistence mode. The docs already said so; the CODE contradicted them by silently defaulting to SQLite outside production. Such a Brain looks healthy — /health ok, chat answering — while the governed qualification routes DO NOT EXIST, because they require the PostgreSQL store. An unconfigured Brain now REFUSES to start. SQLite remains only as an explicitly named TEST-ONLY adapter whose own reason string says 'ungoverned, never canonical'. Owner ruling 2026-09-01.
rules.🚨 releaseIdentityInEvidence: NO LIVE-PRODUCT EVIDENCE IS VALID UNLESS THE EXACT RUNNING RELEASE IDENTITY IS CAPTURED WITH IT. "Tested live" means "tested live against release X, commit Y" — never merely "I opened the product". Owner standard, added 2026-09-04 after a fix that was committed, tested, mutation-proven and pushed was invisible to the person testing the product because production had been serving a build from three days earlier. A truthful harness still produced a false sense of readiness, because nothing in the loop ever asked what was running. Deployment provenance is part of acceptance evidence, not an operational afterthought.

deviationsFromPOSTGRES_CUTOVER_ACCEPTANC: rolcreaterole is TRUE. The acceptance doc specifies LOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOREPLICATION. Everything else matches (super=f, createdb=f, replication=f, bypassrls=f). On PostgreSQL 16 a CREATEROLE role may only administer roles it created, so this is not the pre-16 escalate-to-any-role hole — but it is still not least privilege, and it is not what the spec says. One-line fix: ALTER ROLE migrapilot_brain NOCREATEROLE. The Brain runs schema migrations inside its own database and does not create roles, so there is no functional impact.

The claimed pg_hba restriction to 10.10.0.13/32 + 100.95.14.29/32 DOES NOT EXIST in production. pg_hba_file_rules contains no rule naming the brain database or role at all. The Brain is admitted by two catch-alls: line 141 'host all all 100.64.0.0/10 scram-sha-256' (the whole tailnet) and line 154 'host all all 10.10.0.0/24 scram-sha-256'. Password auth is still required, so possession of the DSN is the real boundary — but the network boundary is much broader than the acceptance document asserts.
phase3Measured.crossDatabaseReach: The role can CONNECT to 22 other databases on db-core (migrapanel, migrapay_billing, migracredit, mpanel, ...) because those databases leave the default PUBLIC CONNECT in place. Measured impact is a metadata surface, NOT a data surface: application tables readable in migrapay_billing, migrapanel, migracredit and migrapilot is ZERO in each. This is a server-wide default that applies to every role, not something the Brain introduced. An initial count of 188 'readable tables' was a measurement artifact — it was counting pg_catalog/information_schema grants, identical in every database.
phase3Measured.alsoNoted: migrapilot_brain_test carries CREATEDB and CREATEROLE — more privileged than the production role.
phase3Measured.verdict: Dedicated database + dedicated non-shared role: CONFIRMED. Least privilege: NOT met, on one role attribute plus a network boundary that is broader than documented. Owner decision required before target A widens access.

tailnetIdentityGate.status: PROVEN_LIVE 2026-09-01. Deployed as release identgate-09020310 (rollback ident-09020230, then gov-09012017).
tailnetIdentityGate.problem: Serving the Brain over the tailnet made it reachable by every node on it. Measured: mail-core and voip-core — a mail server and a VoIP box — both returned 200 on /health.
tailnetIdentityGate.whyNotAnAcl: Tailscale's policy model is default-deny with explicit ACCEPTS and no deny rule, so a permissive tailnet cannot have a single port carved out of it. Tightening would mean re-enumerating every rule across 8+ production servers, with real lockout risk. An earlier report called the ACL 'the mechanism' — that was wrong and is withdrawn.
tailnetIdentityGate.spoofTested: mail-core sent its own Tailscale-User-Login header and arrived with NO identity: Serve overrides client-supplied identity headers. A proxied request also cannot hide by omitting x-forwarded-for, because Serve sets it.
tailnetIdentityGate.trustCondition: Holds only while the Brain is loopback-bound and Serve is the sole route in. Stated in code at the point of use.

outcomeOrchestration.principle: Surface is not capability. Authority is capability.
outcomeOrchestration.shipped: Typed outcome plans (packages/shared-types/src/outcomePlan.ts), a project authority model (projectAuthority.ts) and the dispatcher that consumes them (apps/brain-service/src/engine/orchestration/outcomeDispatcher.ts).
outcomeOrchestration.parentObjectivePreserved: A child result is intermediate context unless its step is marked terminal. This is the defect that answered a build request with a description of a screenshot.
outcomeOrchestration.provenancePerChild: parent turn id, capability requested, selected family, executed backend, tool authority, outcome, failure.
outcomeOrchestration.provenTest: The SAME plan runs to completion under a VS Code workspace and under a connected repo with an identical step sequence; with no authority it stops exactly at workspace.inspect; read-only stops exactly at changeset.propose after inspection succeeded.
outcomeOrchestration.consumerToday: Declares NO_AUTHORITY, so a build is refused with the missing prerequisite AND the blocking step named. Verified live. It becomes capable when a repo authority is connected — no code change in the routing.
outcomeOrchestration.bothSurfacesOnOneContract: The extension now routes from the SAME typed plan as the consumer. It previously decided locally, and the drift produced OPPOSITE bugs from one cause: the consumer answered a build request with a description, while the extension entered the workspace agent whenever an image had yielded a design spec — so a "what is in this image?" turn was dragged into the build path. A spec existing is not a reason to build. Pinned by a regression test across six acceptance cases, which also checks the plain no-image workspace path still reaches the agent.
outcomeOrchestration.brainDecidesRouting: POST /api/ai/orchestrate is the single routing decision. Clients submit objective, attachment MIME types and the project authority they hold; they receive the step sequence, which step is terminal, whether it is executable, and the failure boundary. `surface` is provenance only and is NOT read when deciding.

Separately, the client returned on the `final` frame and the server always sends `final` before `done`, so the frame carrying model/policy/fallback was never read — which also made healthy runs log "stream ended without a done frame".

openDefects.symptom: "use the mockup draft and build this page exactly as it is." with the mockup attached and read: the agent ran ONE workspace.find for index.html,styles.css,app.js, found nothing, and answered "I have not created or proposed any files yet. Please provide more details or clarify your request." No files proposed.
openDefects.evidence: Live in the extension panel, 2026-09-03 03:09 (engineer request 9f2a02ca). Reproduced deterministically before any fix: 2 model calls, no correction, no decision event.
openDefects.rootCause: TWO defects met. (1) The guard against handing work back was gated on `toolStepCount === 0`, so a single search disabled every correction below it — including the directive written for exactly this ending. (2) The controller's intent was hard-coded 'UNKNOWN' and the design spec was concatenated onto the user's message by the client, so nothing downstream could tell a turn that CAME WITH its requirement from one that lacked it.
openDefects.status: DEPLOYED (release admission-09040433), BRAIN-SIDE BEHAVIOUR RE-VERIFIED AFTER THE REFACTOR, PANEL ACCEPTANCE STILL OWED — NOT PROVEN_LIVE.
openDefects.regressionTest: apps/brain-service/test/buildFromSpecification.test.ts (5 cases, incl. openDefects.deployOrder: 🚨 BRAIN FIRST. A new client against an old Brain sends a specification nothing reads, and the spec is DROPPED — strictly worse than the defect. Old client + new Brain is safe (today's behaviour).
openDefects.guardrail: The fix is gated on the turn HOLDING a specification. With none, Record #1 ("build me a website" -> "what kind?" overruled into three unwanted file creations) stays fixed and its test is unchanged. Authority stays READ_ONLY: one re-prompt, never permission to write.
openDefects.deployProof: Brain: the live endpoint rejected an oversized `designSpec` BY NAME and BY BOUND (400 INVALID_INPUT, path designSpec, max 20000) — a field that exists only in the new build; the old one strips unknown keys and proceeds. A valid designSpec passes (only rootPath flagged). Extension: the INSTALLED bundle carries designSpec and keeps the constructor-before-wiring order.
openDefects.deployNotes: Built from a CLEAN worktree check — which FAILED and exposed a separate defect (see repo-hygiene entry). Fell back to the working tree only after proving all 14 rag/*.js build outputs are byte-identical (md5) to what was already deployed, so the in-progress file-attachment lane added nothing new to production.
openDefects.liveEvidence: 2026-09-03, live Brain + real qwen2.5-coder:14b, task 'use the mockup draft and build this page exactly as it is.' with a designSpec. The agent called fs.proposeChangeset ON STEP 1 with complete file content (index.html, full DOCTYPE) — it did NOT search for the files and did NOT ask the user to restate the design, which is the exact failure being fixed. ⚠️ HONEST SCOPE: this exercised the PROMPT half of the fix (the specification block telling the model the spec IS the requirement). The deferral guard never fired because the model never deferred, so that half remains proven by unit tests only. The run then failed at tool execution because the curl harness omitted `clientWorkspaceTools`, so the Brain tried to run the changeset on VM111 instead of delegating it. Logs show delegated fs.proposeChangeset succeeding (138ms, outcome ok) on extension-driven runs. The harness was wrong, not the product. RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-04 on release admission-09040433 with real qwen2.5-coder:14b: the agent again called fs.proposeChangeset on STEP 1 with complete file content, no search and no deferral, and emitted no false "no tool ran" footer. The engine/ regrouping and the admission module did not change the behaviour.

openDefects.symptom: Every grounded chat turn ends in "The engine could not complete the request" after ~240s while ComfyUI holds the GPU.
openDefects.evidence: nvidia-smi: 23723/24576 MiB used, utilization.gpu 100%, 69C, with ComfyUI /queue reporting 1 running job. Ollama /api/ps shows qwen3:8b RESIDENT at 11.5GB, so this is not a model-load failure. A direct /api/generate probe for the trivial prompt "Reply with exactly the word: READY" hung past 600s, proving the stall is in generation and is upstream of MigraPilot. Substituting the smaller qwen2.5vl:7b failed identically, so model size is not the variable.
openDefects.rootCause: Unarbitrated GPU sharing between ComfyUI (image) and Ollama (chat) on one 24GB card.
openDefects.status: PRODUCT BEHAVIOUR FIXED AND DEPLOYED 2026-09-04 (release admission-09040433, rollback repro-09030600). The environmental cause stands; what is fixed is that the product no longer answers it with a 240s wait and a generic failure.
openDefects.regressionTest: apps/brain-service/test/engineerCapacityGate.test.ts (refuses before any model call; does NOT refuse a card that still answers), plus rewritten cases in gpuCapacity.test.ts.
openDefects.liveAcceptance: Blocked until the card is free.
correctedClaims: CORRECTED: "two ComfyUI instances on :8188". There is ONE ComfyUI — PID 42312 (launcher), PID 23820 (worker, listening 127.0.0.1:8188), PID 41308 (comfy-tailscale-bridge.py, listening 100.86.143.93:8188). Nothing is redundant, so there is no spare instance to stop.

CORRECTED: "EASY to unblock by stopping a ComfyUI instance". ComfyUI was mid-render (/queue reported 1 running job), so stopping it would destroy in-flight owner work. The safe path is to wait for the queue to drain.

REFINED: "VRAM exhaustion" is not the whole mechanism. Generation stalls with the model already resident and with a smaller model substituted, and the card reads 100% utilisation — so compute contention matters, not just memory headroom.
openDefects.measuredContrast: Same conversation, same question, same model: NO answer in >5 minutes at 24.0/24.5 GB and 100% util; "Red" in 15 s at 5.7 GB and 11%. The failure is resource starvation, not prompting or routing.
openDefects.slice1: TRUTHFUL READINESS + BOUNDED WAIT SHIPPED (brain capacity2-08271948). The worst part — accepting work the system cannot execute — is closed. Arbitration/scheduling is slice 2 and is NOT built: nothing evicts models, kills renders, or moves workloads.
openDefects.fix: THREE gaps, each measured. (a) engineerRoutes consulted GPU capacity ZERO times — the chat path had gated on it for a while, the coding agent never did, which is why a build-from-mockup turn burned the full 240s provider deadline. It now refuses before any model call. (b) gpuCapacity returned `ready` the moment a model was resident, short-circuiting the render check; measured, a resident 15.3GB model beside a render did not answer in 180s while /health said ready. Residency now keeps its fast path only when nothing is competing; otherwise one token is requested and the answer decides. (c) ComfyUI going silent was read as an idle card, when its /queue had stopped answering BECAUSE a render was blocking its event loop.
openDefects.note2026_09_06: STILL OPEN and environmental, not a code defect. Re-triggered on 2026-09-06 by running the MigraAI Studio framing A/B on this workstation: ComfyUI held ~16GB of the 3090 that production inference shares, leaving 8GB — enough for qwen3:8b and qwen2.5vl:7b, NOT for qwen3-coder:30b (migra-forge). ComfyUI Desktop AND its separate python server were stopped; killing the Electron shell alone does not release the VRAM. Standing implication: Studio rendering and MigraPilot production inference must not share this GPU concurrently.

openDefects.title: A single vision read of a mockup silently drops whole regions
openDefects.symptom: Eight reads of the SAME mockup through the governed path returned the full 9-element set five times; the others dropped regions (sidebar, card heading), once falling to 3/9. Output length barely moved (1231 chars for both a 5/9 and a 9/9 read), so this is omission, not truncation.
openDefects.evidence: Measured live against qwen2.5vl:7b via the production Brain, 8 runs then 6 runs.
openDefects.rootCause: Model non-determinism. The chat path exposes no temperature, top_p or seed at the route or provider layer, so the variance cannot be turned down — only caught.
openDefects.mitigation: A second pass asks the model what its own transcription is missing, with the image still in front of it. Across 6 runs the worst case improved from 3/9 to 8/9 and no run dropped a region. Mean is still below 9/9, so a complex design can lose detail.
openDefects.liveAcceptance: Re-measure element carry-through when a determinism knob or a stronger vision model lands.

openDefects.title: 🚨 The remote Brain cannot see the developer's workspace
openDefects.severity: CRITICAL — blocks the coding-assistant north star
openDefects.symptom: An attached mockup reaches the agent, the agent calls fs.proposeChangeset, and the tool fails. The final answer says nothing was created — which is at least truthful.
openDefects.rootCause: Workspace tools execute on the BRAIN HOST's filesystem. The Brain now runs on VM111; the developer's files are on the workstation. Proven by control: the identical fs.proposeChangeset call with rootPath=/tmp (which exists on VM111) SUCCEEDS, while the workstation path fails, and that path does not exist on VM111.
openDefects.scope: 16 capabilities read the workspace: diagnostics.get, edit.apply, edit.preview, file.read, file.readRange, file.readSymbol, fs.applyChangeset, fs.proposeChangeset, git.blame, git.diff, git.history, git.overview, git.status, workspace.find, workspace.list, workspace.search. Measured: git.status and file.read return TOOL_FAILED; workspace.list returned a SILENT EMPTY.
openDefects.notCausedByTargetA: This is not the HTTPS switch. The SSH tunnel pointed at the same remote Brain, so the breakage arrived with the Brain migration itself and was simply never exercised by a coding turn until now.
openDefects.partialFixShipped: The silent-empty is fixed and deployed (release rootguard-09020400): a missing ROOT now fails loudly and explains that workspace tools read the Brain host's filesystem. That stops the agent being told its project is empty and inventing files, but it does NOT restore the capability.
optionsForOwner: A. Execute workspace tools EXTENSION-SIDE. The Brain plans; the extension performs filesystem work locally and returns results. This is how Claude Code and Copilot actually work, keeps one governed Brain, and needs no credentials or code on the workstation. Largest change: a tool-execution callback.

B. Run a Brain process ON THE WORKSTATION pointed at the governed db-core PostgreSQL. Files resolve, and there is still exactly ONE governed database. Cost: the DSN lives on the workstation, and there are two Brain processes against one store.
C. Sync or mount the workspace onto VM111. Copies the developer's source to a server; heaviest, and raises data-location questions.
openDefects.recommendation: A is the correct architecture; B is the pragmatic interim that keeps governance intact.
openDefects.status: FIXED and COMPLETE — 16/16 tools execute (release toolsurface-09020630)
openDefects.fix: Option A: the client runs the workspace tools. Brain emits event: tool_request over the existing SSE stream; the extension executes locally and POSTs to /api/ai/engineer/tool-result. Client-initiated throughout, so no inbound path to a developer machine is needed, and the agent loop is unchanged — it awaits executeTool as before and cannot tell where the work ran.
openDefects.provenLive: A file planted seconds earlier with an unguessable name (zz-marker-7741.txt), existing ONLY on the workstation, was named back by the agent running on VM111. It could not have been guessed. Delegated calls in that run: workspace.list and fs.proposeChangeset, both executed by the compiled extension module.
openDefects.safety: Every delegated call settles: a deadline per call, disposal on stream close AND on completion, and a timeout surfaces as a tool FAILURE — never an empty success. Delegation is opt-in so an older client cannot deadlock. Client tools propose without writing and contain paths to the root.
openDefects.toolSurface: COMPLETE — 16/16. The canonical registry in @migrapilot/workspace-tools now declares all 16 with mutation/approval/dry-run classified in ONE place; the brain's delegation allowlist and the client's routing both derive from it. The tree/file/git implementations MOVED into that package and the brain re-exports them, so both sides run the same functions. diagnostics.get and file.readSymbol get a VS Code adapter — better there than on a server (real language servers, not one parser) and it keeps the TypeScript compiler out of the bundle.

driftControl.assumption: MinIO data shares cloud-core's 32GB OS filesystem, so media growth would fill the OS disk.
driftControl.disprovedBy: MINIO_VOLUMES=/mnt/client-storage — a dedicated 200GB disk, 175GB free. I had measured / instead of MinIO's configured volume.

driftControl.assumption: There is no off-host backup of anything.
driftControl.disprovedBy: PBS CT 9002 runs a daily restic backup of the whole datastore to Hetzner Object Storage (192GiB), plus a weekly restore drill.
driftControl.corrected: An off-host copy existed; the gap was object granularity, not existence.

driftControl.assumption: Follow-up image context is broken — every follow-up is answered blind.
driftControl.disprovedBy: Consumer trace showed requested:1 sent:0 dropped:1 — the artifact had been deleted by me minutes earlier. A clean test showed sent:1 and has_image:true.
driftControl.corrected: Follow-up image context works. No second mechanism was built.

driftControl.assumption: The PDF upload rejection is a bug/regression.
driftControl.disprovedBy: storage.ts deliberately excludes pdf/docx/xlsx with a comment explaining that accepting them would fabricate a capability.
driftControl.corrected: It is an intentional honest refusal; the work is building extraction.

driftControl.assumption: Backups for VM103 were weekly (5 snapshots).
driftControl.disprovedBy: My own head -6 truncation. Real: 11 snapshots, daily, 6-10s incremental.
systemctl EnvironmentFiles — brain-postgres.env loads after brain.env and wins.

driftControl.assumption: A green pre-commit hook means the build is green.
driftControl.disprovedBy: Hook runs tsc --noEmit; the suite runs tsc -b. A committed test broke npm test.
driftControl.corrected: Acceptance gate is the app's own test command + tsc -b + live browser.

driftControl.assumption: A conversation that predates a feature will show its new UI once the feature ships.
driftControl.disprovedBy: A pre-fileRefs conversation showed no historical card after detach — the record was never written for turns stored before M21.
driftControl.corrected: Historical cards exist only for turns stored after the feature. Not a regression; older threads have no record to render.

driftControl.assumption: My brain deploy broke the turn path — two turns returned no_output straight after it.
driftControl.disprovedBy: Rolled the brain back; turns still failed. Then tested the model host directly: every model returns "unexpected EOF" standalone, with MigraPilot out of the picture.
driftControl.corrected: The change was innocent and has been rolled forward. The fault is the workstation Ollama runner.

driftControl.assumption: "Ollama is inactive" — read from `systemctl is-active ollama` on VM111.
driftControl.disprovedBy: VM111 has no local Ollama; the model runs on the workstation at 100.86.143.93:11434, which returns HTTP 200.
driftControl.corrected: Measured the wrong host. The same wrong-endpoint pattern as the MinIO disk misread.

driftControl.assumption: Every model on the workstation fails with "unexpected EOF" — the Ollama runner is broken.
driftControl.disprovedBy: The Ollama log showed those POSTs returning HTTP 400, not 500. "unexpected EOF" was Ollama failing to PARSE my request body, mangled by nested quoting through ssh -> qm guest exec -> sh -c -> curl. A well-formed request to the same model succeeded immediately.
driftControl.corrected: Ollama was healthy the whole time. The real fault is VRAM contention with ComfyUI, which affects large models only. I restarted Ollama on the basis of the wrong diagnosis; it was harmless but unnecessary.

driftControl.claim: "Active image resolution already works — the defect is purely intent."
driftControl.verdict: DISPROVEN FOR GENERATED IMAGES. True for uploads.
driftControl.detail: The conversation's active image set was populated only from resolved ATTACHMENTS — setConversationImages was never called with what a turn GENERATED. So an uploaded picture could be referred to as "it" and a picture MigraPilot had just drawn could not. Half the statement was correct, which is why reading the code confirmed it.
driftControl.howItSurfaced: Only because the intent fix was deployed FIRST and the reported sentence still reproduced verbatim. With the routing correct and the behaviour unchanged, the remaining cause had nowhere left to hide.
driftControl.lesson: A partially true claim survives code reading, because the half you check is the half that holds. Fixing one cause and re-testing is what separates them.

driftControl.claim: "Vision is not approved on production (approved: []) — Phase 8 is blocked."
driftControl.verdict: STALE / WRONG. Production already enforces a governed vision decision.
driftControl.detail: /api/ai/vision-registry on production returns enforced=true with vision.general qualified to qwen2.5vl:7b against an exact digest, and names it as the model an image turn would actually use. A first probe appeared to show a fail-closed null only because it read keys ('byState', 'defaultDecision') the route does not emit — the real keys are 'registry' and 'default'. The registry was right; the probe was wrong.
driftControl.corrected: Phase 8 recorded as satisfied on production, verified live with a real image.

driftControl.claim: "A spare-port boot test proves a Brain release works under production configuration."
driftControl.verdict: DISPROVEN. Those boot tests never loaded the production environment.
driftControl.detail: /etc/migrapilot/*.env is root-only, so 'sudo -u migrapilot bash -c . brain.env' sourced NOTHING and the candidate booted on defaults. Older builds silently fell back to SQLite, so the test passed while proving almost nothing; the new fail-closed persistence rule is what exposed it, by refusing to start. Releases are now swapped through systemd, which reads the env as root, with a named rollback target.
driftControl.corrected: Boot-test claims downgraded; deploy verification is post-swap health + readiness axes.

driftControl.verdict: PARTLY FALSE. The document asserts a pg_hba restriction production does not have.
driftControl.detail: The doc states pg_hba is limited to 10.10.0.13/32 and 100.95.14.29/32 with scram-sha-256. pg_hba_file_rules has no rule naming the brain database or role; access comes from 'host all all 100.64.0.0/10' and 'host all all 10.10.0.0/24'. The role also carries CREATEROLE where the doc says NOCREATEROLE. Treat that document as the INTENT of the cutover, not as evidence of the current boundary.
driftControl.corrected: Phase 3 now records measured catalog facts; the acceptance doc is demoted to intent.

driftControl.claim: "A Tailscale ACL is the mechanism for restricting the served Brain port."
driftControl.verdict: WRONG, withdrawn. Tailscale has no deny rule.
driftControl.detail: The policy model is default-deny with explicit accepts, so you cannot except one port from a permissive tailnet — you must replace the blanket accept and enumerate everything, across every production server, with lockout risk. The boundary was expressible in the application instead: require a tailnet USER identity, which Serve supplies for user-owned nodes and withholds for tagged servers.
driftControl.corrected: Implemented as a Brain-side identity gate; ACL restructuring left as an optional separate lane.

driftControl.claim: "The engineer path broke — PROVIDER_CONNECT_TIMEOUT after the delegation change."
driftControl.verdict: NOT CAUSED BY THE CHANGE. Transient cold-model load.
driftControl.detail: An engineer run failed with a 240s connect timeout to the Ollama provider, which looked like a regression. Two controls disproved it: the same request with clientWorkspaceTools=false failed identically, and once qwen2.5-coder:14b (15GB) was resident both succeeded. A separate false step: Ollama appeared unreachable on its tailnet IP when probed FROM WSL, but the Brain connects from VM111, where it answered in 0.26s — the wrong vantage point, not a fault.
driftControl.corrected: Provider timeouts under cold load are a capacity signal, not evidence about the delegation path.

driftControl.claim: "A systemd drop-in with Environment= overrides a value set in an EnvironmentFile."
driftControl.verdict: FALSE. EnvironmentFile= takes precedence over Environment=, whatever the order.
driftControl.detail: A drop-in setting Environment=MIGRAPILOT_PROVIDER_URL was merged, sorted last, and reported as set by `systemctl show` — while the Brain kept using brain.env's value. The only honest check was behavioural: the model catalog stayed at 16 instead of collapsing to the pod's 1. Overriding an env-file value requires another EnvironmentFile listed last.
driftControl.corrected: Remote-provider overrides now use an EnvironmentFile drop-in, verified by catalog size.

pdfQualification.ranOn: 2026-08-27. Nine fixtures, three candidates, verdicts kept separate by layer.
pdfQualification.fixtures: Built rather than assumed: clean text, 5-page multipage, headings/order, table, mixed text+image (Chrome headless); image-only via ghostscript rasterisation and VERIFIED to have no text layer (pdftotext returns nothing); encrypted via pypdf; malformed by truncating a valid PDF so the xref is destroyed; and a real 26-page 116KB document.

layerVerdicts.textExtraction: ALL THREE correct on every text fixture.
layerVerdicts.readingOrder: ALL THREE preserved order across h1/h2/h3/paragraph sequences.
layerVerdicts.headingsSections: NONE preserve heading LEVEL. All three return flat text — headings survive as ordered lines, not as structure. Any heading awareness would be ours to build downstream.
layerVerdicts.tables: unpdf preserves ROW structure as lines ("EMEA Q2 9930.25 Rivera") — usable as-is. pdfjs-dist returns cell-level items WITH coordinates, so columns can be reconstructed precisely but only with work. pdf-parse sits between. No library returns a real table model.
layerVerdicts.pageBoundariesMetadata: ALL THREE report page counts correctly (5/5 and 26/26). pdf-parse also emits explicit "-- N of M --" separators.
layerVerdicts.scannedDetection: 🚨 THE SHARPEST DIFFERENCE. unpdf and pdfjs-dist return EXACTLY 0 characters on an image-only PDF, so "no text layer" is detectable. pdf-parse returns 12 characters of SYNTHETIC page separator ("-- 1 of 1 --"), so a naive empty-text check silently concludes the page has text. Adopting pdf-parse would require stripping its decorations before any scanned check.
layerVerdicts.encrypted: ALL THREE throw PasswordException("No password given") — clear, identical, actionable.
layerVerdicts.malformed: ALL THREE throw InvalidPDFException("Invalid PDF structure") — fails safely, no partial text.
layerVerdicts.cpuMemory: Comparable. 26-page real document: unpdf 188ms, pdfjs-dist 227ms, pdf-parse 172ms. Peak heap ~11MB.
layerVerdicts.footprint: unpdf 2.6MB with ZERO dependencies. pdfjs-dist 68MB. pdf-parse 57MB. Both of the latter pull @napi-rs/canvas with a native .node binary.
layerVerdicts.license: unpdf MIT; pdfjs-dist Apache-2.0; pdf-parse Apache-2.0. All commercially usable.
layerVerdicts.deployPathCompatibility: PROVEN ON VM111, not inferred: unpdf installs as 1 package / 2.6MB with ZERO native binaries and extracted correctly on the real runtime. No install scripts on any candidate, so none requires the compiler VM111 lacks — but pdfjs-dist and pdf-parse depend on a prebuilt native canvas binary, which the deploy path can carry only because the install host IS the runtime host.

pdfQualification.recommendation: NOT a single winner. unpdf as the DEFAULT extractor: smallest surface by a wide margin, zero dependencies, no native binary, best out-of-the-box line and table-row fidelity, and honest zero-length output on scanned pages. pdfjs-dist as the ESCALATION path if column-accurate table reconstruction is ever needed, since it exposes per-item coordinates and is the same engine unpdf wraps. pdf-parse NOT adopted: it costs 57MB and a native canvas dependency, and its synthetic page separators actively break the scanned-page check.
pdfQualification.harnessErrorsWorthKeeping: Three of my own probe errors nearly scored two libraries as broken. pdfjs-dist and pdf-parse both need their worker MODULE IMPORTED in Node — setting workerSrc to the file path is not enough and produces a version-mismatch that reads exactly like a broken package. pdf-parse v2 exposes a PDFParse CLASS, not v1's default function. And its worker must be imported by FILE URL because its exports map blocks the deep specifier. Separately, my assertion normalised whitespace and so reported a missing anchor that was really the PDF's own line wrap ("ANCHOR-TEXT-\nOMEGA") — the fixture's wrapping, measured as if it were the parser's fidelity.

speechOutputQualification.haitianCreole: NOT AVAILABLE in either — Piper ships 56 locales, Kokoro 9, and Creole is in neither. It needs a trained voice, which is its own program rather than part of shipping speech output. French is the nearest neighbour and is not a substitute.
speechOutputQualification.whatRemains: Both are permissive, self-hosted, CPU-only, no paid dependency, no new GPU contention. The numbers cannot decide it: Piper is far lighter and ~10x faster to first word; Kokoro is generally judged more natural for ~1 s and 2 GB. Bonex listens, then integration begins.
speechOutputQualification.⭐ readUnderTheProductStandard: The standard forbids choosing an engine because it is easier on TODAY'S hardware. Piper's advantage is 358 MB vs 2.1 GB and ~1 s of latency — both are hardware-scale concerns that a real deployment target erases, and Kokoro already needs no GPU. So the choice must be made on VOICE QUALITY at production scale; if Kokoro sounds materially better, its second of latency is a performance constraint to record, not a reason to ship the weaker voice.

decision.primary: Kokoro (Apache-2.0) — chosen on voice quality, which is the only axis the product standard allows here.
decision.fallback: Piper (MIT) — much lighter and faster; the low-resource route, never the primary voice.
decision.🚨 engineNamesAreInternal: Users never see "Kokoro" or "Piper". MigraPilot offers polished VOICE CHOICES; a routing layer decides which qualified engine serves them. That keeps the engine replaceable without a product change and stops an implementation detail leaking into the UI.
productPath: playback starts quickly (sentence-split; measured 1,243 ms to first audio)
text answer survives if synthesis fails
no fake playback state after reload
decision.acceptance: Bonex listens INSIDE MigraPilot, not to qualification samples. Only then PROVEN_LIVE.

speechOutputSlice.architecture: Synthesis lives in the EXISTING speech runtime (services/speech-runtime) beside ASR — same process, same auth, same capability seam. A second service would have meant a second secret, a second unit and a second thing to forget to start. The Brain owns the capability and delegates, so moving synthesis to a bigger machine later is a URL change, not a redesign.
speechOutputSlice.🚨 engineIdentityStrippedAtTheBoundary: The runtime reports which engine spoke and why it fell back; the Brain strips those fields in ONE place before the product sees anything. Verified live: the product response carries no underscore-prefixed field. No consumer can grow a dependency on a name it never receives, which is what keeps the engine replaceable.
speechOutputSlice.measuredOnCpu: Warm RTF 0.41-0.44 — a 7.5 s answer synthesises in ~3 s. 2.3 GB resident for whisper AND Kokoro together. No GPU touched.

liveProof.controlPresent: Read aloud appears on assistant answers
liveProof.playback: preparing -> playing -> ended -> idle, driven by the real HTMLAudioElement
liveProof.stop: mid-playback stop returns the control to idle immediately
liveProof.reload: control is idle; NO false playing/preparing state, no lingering error, answer intact
liveProof.failure: 413 "That answer is too long to read aloud in one go." and the answer survived untouched

speechOutputSlice.noFakeState: Audio is not persisted, and that is the honest choice rather than a shortcut: after a reload there IS no audio, so the control is idle. Restoring a play-ready control for audio that no longer exists is exactly the false state the rule forbids.
speechOutputSlice.stillOwed: Bonex listens INSIDE MigraPilot. Until then this is not PROVEN_LIVE.
speechOutputSlice.knownConstraint: HARDWARE, recorded not compensated for: synthesis is whole-answer, so the wait is ~0.4x the spoken length. Sentence-streaming would cut it to ~1.2 s regardless of answer length and is the next increment — the slice is complete within its defined scope, not disguised as finished.

🚨 acceptanceIsBonexEarsOnly.rule: The remaining gate is HUMAN PERCEPTUAL ACCEPTANCE in the real product — voice quality, intelligibility, pacing, pronunciation, startup delay, and whether Read aloud feels natural enough to keep enabled. Implementation evidence does NOT substitute, and the agent must not self-certify any of the three outcomes.

outcomes.PROVEN_LIVE: Warm is good enough as shipped.
outcomes.IMPLEMENTED_NEEDS_VOICE_TUNING: Plumbing correct; voice or pacing not acceptable.
outcomes.IMPLEMENTED_NEEDS_LATENCY_WORK: The whole-answer startup materially hurts the experience.

speechOutputSlice.nonPersistenceAccepted: Bonex confirmed: the synthesised artifact is ephemeral, so returning to idle after reload is TRUTHFUL. Persisting a phantom "ready" state would be worse than deliberately starting clean.
speechOutputSlice.warmupAddedBeforeTheGate: The engine now loads in a background thread at runtime startup (measured 4,339 ms). Without it the first Read aloud after any restart paid that on top of synthesis — which would have made a LATENCY judgement about a cold start rather than about the product. Steady state is RTF ~0.47.
speechOutputSlice.🚨 affordanceFailedOnFirstContact: Shipped as a bare speaker icon among the secondary actions. The first person to use it reported the feature had "no play option" — WHILE IT WAS WORKING. Two causes, both mine: a speaker glyph reads as volume/mute rather than "play this", and an unlabelled spinner through several seconds of synthesis looks like nothing happened. Now a play triangle, the word "Listen", and a visible "Preparing audio…". A capability nobody can find is not shipped.
speechOutputSlice.🚨 measuredLatencyInTheProduct: CLICK TO AUDIO: 8.5 s for a two-sentence answer, measured through the real UI — worse than the ~3.7 s runtime figure because the product number includes MP3 encode, two service hops and blob handling. This is direct evidence for the IMPLEMENTED_NEEDS_LATENCY_WORK outcome. The agent does NOT get to decide that; it is reported for Bonex to judge against how it actually feels.
speechOutputSlice.latencyFixIfNeeded: Sentence-streaming: synthesise and play the first sentence while the rest continues. Measured first-audio would drop to ~1.2 s REGARDLESS of answer length. Not built — it is a real increment, not a tweak, and it should follow the listening judgement rather than pre-empt it.
speechOutputSlice.🚨 falseGreenMyTestEnvironmentHid: Playback worked under Playwright and did NOTHING in Bonex's real browser. `audio.play()` was called after two awaits on a brand-new element the user had never touched — browsers revoke audio permission across an async gap, and synthesis takes seconds, so the gesture was always long gone. Test automation runs a permissive autoplay policy, so my environment differed from the user's in EXACTLY the way that mattered. He only heard it because MY automated click played through the workstation speakers.
speechOutputSlice.gestureFix: The element is now created and started on a one-sample SILENT clip synchronously inside the click, before any await, then the real audio is swapped into that same element. Permission belongs to an element the user has already played. If a stricter browser still refuses, the state becomes "Play" — the audio exists and is ready, and the next click is a fresh gesture that always works. Reporting a failure there would be wrong: nothing failed except the timing of a permission.
speechOutputSlice.bonexPerceptualFeedbackSoFar: Heard the voice (female English) and called it CLEAN. That is positive on the voice-quality axis but does NOT close the gate — he had not been able to trigger it himself, so pacing, startup delay and whether it feels worth keeping enabled are still unjudged.
speechOutputSlice.ACCEPTED: ✅ PROVEN_LIVE 2026-08-27. Outcome: the first of the three — Warm is good enough as shipped. Bonex triggered it from his own browser after the gesture fix and judged it good; he did NOT call for latency work, so the ~8.5 s whole-answer start is accepted for now and sentence-streaming stays available as a future increment rather than a required one.

messageFeedbackSlice.schema: M24 message_feedback, PK (owner, workspace, conversation, message) — update/retract are natural rather than bolted on. FORCE RLS; tenant isolation asserted in tests.
messageFeedbackSlice.engineerSeam: schema_version plus turn provenance (request/model/provider/turnContext) travel with every record so a later evaluation pipeline reads them without a migration. Those fields CANNOT be back-filled: by the time anyone wants them the turn is gone. Building the consumer is a different slice.
messageFeedbackSlice.notAControl: Feedback never edits, regenerates or re-ranks. A button that silently changed your answer would be worse than one that did nothing.
messageFeedbackSlice.noOptimisticUpdate: The UI updates only after the server agrees. An optimistic update would recreate the original defect in subtler form — a thumb that looks saved while the write failed.

pickerStorageAgreement.canonicalDefinition: src/features/attachments/capability.ts — picker accept, storage allowlist, refusal copy and GET /api/files/capability all derive from it. Separate hand-maintained lists were the defect.

classification.indexed_35: pdf, docx, and every plain-text document/data/code type the indexer genuinely reads — verified per-extension against Exclusions, not assumed.
classification.refused_13: Office binaries and Open Document (no extractor), archives (containers), sql (indexer treats it as a dump).
classification.xlsx_pptx_held_deliberately: Refused for a REASON, not for want of a parser: spreadsheet ANALYSIS is a known open defect, and shipping ingestion on top of it would advertise a capability that answers confidently and wrongly.
classification.expandedWhereItGenuinelyWorks: c, h, cpp, cs, php, swift, kt, tsv added — plain text the indexer already reads. Correcting an under-inclusive list, not blind expansion.

pickerStorageAgreement.smugglingGapFoundLive: A zip renamed to .csv was ACCEPTED (200) during the acceptance run: the validator trusted the extension and never read the bytes. It would have stored an archive as text, been skipped by the indexer at its first NUL byte, and sat in the library looking accepted. Closed with a content check on text-shaped types ONLY. PDF and DOCX are legitimately binary with real extractors, so the rule is: no binary wearing a text file name — not: no binary.

liveAcceptance.4_smuggling: zip-as-csv 400 after the fix, 200 before it
liveAcceptance.5_server_authoritative: every refusal enforced server-side with the picker bypassed entirely
liveAcceptance.7_no_regression: docx 200; the image path is separate and untouched

unifiedAttachments.fiveAllowlistsFound: capability.ts, storage ALLOWED, filename.ts rejectionFor, Composer ACCEPTED_IMAGE_TYPES, and images.ts IMAGE_EXTENSIONS — plus two separate accept attributes. My earlier claim that "one list decides what MigraPilot accepts" covered three of them and was overstated.
unifiedAttachments.architecture: The picker SELECTS; the system CLASSIFIES. One handler reads the first 512 bytes of every chosen file, classifies by extension + MIME + signature, and dispatches to the image or document pipeline. Action Hub entries are filters over that same handler.
unifiedAttachments.noCustomFiles: The general attach input carries NO accept attribute, so the native dialog reads "All Files" rather than "Custom Files" — HTML offers no way to NAME a filter group, so this is the closest honest label. Nothing is filtered out before classification.
unifiedAttachments.🚨 aTestCaughtABugIIntroduced: Adding images to INDEXED_EXTENSIONS made the DOCUMENT store accept PNGs, because storage derived its allowlist from every selectable type. An existing test — "formats the indexer cannot read are refused" — failed and was right. One contract does not mean one bucket: DOCUMENT_EXTENSIONS and IMAGE_EXTENSIONS_CANONICAL now derive per pipeline.
unifiedAttachments.testsUpdatedNotDeleted: Six tests asserted the old architecture. One of them literally asserted that photo.png was an unsupported type — it encoded the bug. Each was rewritten to assert the same INTENT against the new mechanism; the .env protection moved to the classifier rather than disappearing.

attachmentErrorTruthfulness.🚨 defect1_falseNetworkError: A 35.5 MB PDF failed with "The upload could not reach the server" while the server had answered with a classified 413. The catch wrapped BOTH the fetch AND response.json(), so a proxy that rejected the body with an HTML error page became a network fault. Bonex predicted this exact collapse before the code was read.
attachmentErrorTruthfulness.realCause: nginx client_max_body_size on the reverse proxy. Measured by binary search against production: 31.7 MB passes, 32.2 MB returns 413 text/html. The app advertised 1024 MB — it promised a gigabyte down a path that carries ~32 MB.
fixes: fetch failure and parse failure are now separate; only a genuinely unanswered request claims unreachability
a 413 says "That file is too large to upload"; any other status reports the real code
MAX_FILE_BYTES default lowered 1024 -> 31 MB to match the transport, so an oversized file is refused BEFORE a wasted upload
attachmentErrorTruthfulness.🚨 defect2_staleRefusalWasMine: The .wav notice sitting above an unrelated PDF came from MY unified handler routing document refusals into setImageError — one global slot shared with image errors, never cleared on a new selection. Refusals now carry the FILE NAME, render per file, are dismissed individually, and are cleared deterministically when a new selection begins.

liveProof.oversized_real_pdf: "liv_kreyol_AI-Training.pdf / Files are limited to 31 MB." — names the file and the real reason
liveProof.no_false_unreachable: the unreachable copy did not appear
liveProof.reload: no stale errors or attachments resurrected
liveProof.mixed: document route 200; the image path is unchanged and was proven with a real PNG

attachmentErrorTruthfulness.🚨 stillOwedNotInMyScope: The TRANSPORT cause is nginx on VM102, which I could not reach: its guest agent is down and SSH host-key trust is unestablished, and the hook exception covers VM111 only. Raising client_max_body_size there is the real fix for large PDFs; until then 31 MB is the honest limit and MIGRAPILOT_MAX_FILE_MB must be raised with it, never before.

resolvedDefects.severity: HIGH — a wrong figure is asserted to the model as exact arithmetic it must not recalculate
resolvedDefects.symptom: Asked "What is the total Revenue in this file?" over a 9-row CSV, the deterministic table layer computed the sum of the ZIPCODE column (570,236) and injected it as "[Computed directly ... exact arithmetic ... Use them verbatim and do not recalculate them:] sum of \"ZipCode\": 570,236". The model, handed evidence that did not answer the question, footed the table itself and returned $367,500. The true total is 474,000.
resolvedDefects.rootCause: TWO rules meeting. (1) parseTable marks a column quantitative only when >=90% of non-blank cells are quantities. One "n/a" among nine rows put Revenue at 7/8 = 87.5%, so the actual money column was DISQUALIFIED. (2) chooseValueColumn then falls back from "the named column" to "the only quantitative column" — which was ZipCode, because plain 5-digit ZIPs are not caught by the leading-zero identifier rule. The fallback substitutes a DIFFERENT column silently and the evidence block then asserts authority over it.
resolvedDefects.🚨 whyThisIsWorseThanTheOriginal: The module exists because the model footed tables wrong. It now produces a wrong number AND tells the model not to recalculate it. Its own docblock promises "a ZIP code, an order id ... must never be summed"; a ZIP code was summed and presented as the answer to a question about revenue.
resolvedDefects.measuredNotInferred: Run against the product's own modules: Region 0/9, OrderID 0/9 (leading zeros -> identifier, correctly excluded), ZipCode 9/9 = 100% quantitative, Revenue 7/8 = 87.5% -> NOT quantitative. The same parser sums those very Revenue cells to exactly 474,000, so the ARITHMETIC is sound; the COLUMN SELECTION is the defect.
resolvedDefects.provenBothWays: With one character changed — the "n/a" replaced by an empty cell — Revenue clears the threshold (7/7) and the whole path is correct end to end: evidence "sum of \"Revenue\": 474,000 (7 rows used, 2 blank)", model answer "The total Revenue in this file is $474,000", outcome=ok, and the durable record after reload holds the same sentence.
resolvedDefects.status: RESOLVED 2026-09-04 — three rules, each proven by reintroducing it, then re-measured live on the SAME fixture that failed.
resolvedDefects.suggestedDirection: Do not simply lower the threshold. The honest options are (a) refuse rather than substitute: if a NAMED column is disqualified, emit no evidence instead of computing a different column, and (b) let a named column report why it was disqualified. Silence beats a confident wrong figure; substitution is the part that must go.
resolvedDefects.fix: (1) A missing marker (n/a, N/A, null, none, nil, NaN, -, --, em dash, ?) is a BLANK, not text — an absence must not argue against a column being numeric. Revenue goes 7/8=87.5% to 7/7=100%. (2) A NAMED column is never silently swapped: if the question names columns, the answer comes from one of those or from a refusal that names it. (3) A column whose HEADER identifies rather than measures (zip/zipcode/postcode/id/sku/phone…) is not computable however numeric its cells look — matched on TOKENS so "paid" and "grid" are untouched. Where wrong it errs toward refusing, which is the safe direction.
resolvedDefects.refusalIsSpoken: Silence was not enough: going quiet leaves the model holding a table and a question about a total, which is how 473,250 and 367,500 happened. A refusal now carries text telling the model to say so plainly and NOT to add the numbers up itself.
resolvedDefects.reMeasuredLive: Same fixture, same question, real UI: "The total Revenue in this file is $474,000." Not 570,236 (the ZIP sum), not 367,500 (the invented figure), not 473,250 (the historical one). Survives reload. And "What is the sum of the ZipCode column?" now answers "not meaningful or applicable because ZipCodes are identifiers and not numerical values to be summed up."
resolvedDefects.resolutionEvidence: RESOLVED. A named column is never silently swapped for another — the branch now refuses and states why rather than falling through. Pinned by columnSelection.test.ts, written against the measured failure (asked for Revenue, computed ZIPCODE 570,236 and labelled it exact arithmetic).

Rephrasing to "compare every revenue_eur value and state the single largest" produced the correct answer, so it is prompt/model-sensitive rather than retrieval loss.
resolvedDefects.classification: NOT a Files & Documents transport, retrieval or provenance defect. A reasoning/fidelity weakness of qwen3:8b on structured tabular data. Owner ruling 2026-08-27.
resolvedDefects.status: OPEN — separate model/tool-routing quality item; does not hold the document pipeline open.
resolvedDefects.longerTermDirection: Do not rely on an LLM alone for arithmetic over CSV. MigraPilot should detect that a request is a DETERMINISTIC DATA OPERATION, route it through a table/data tool, and let the model explain the result rather than compute it.
resolvedDefects.provenance: Arose from the 9/10 citation pass. That run is preserved verbatim and was NOT rewritten to 10/10.
resolvedDefects.resolutionEvidence: RESOLVED for the arithmetic it describes. The figure is COMPUTED by the deterministic layer and handed to the model as evidence ("Computed directly from … use these figures verbatim"), so the model no longer selects or transcribes the number. resolvedDefects.symptom: GET /api/files/index returned state "approved", searchable true, and stats files=0 chunks=0 with an EMPTY chunkCounts map. Grounded turns then told the user "No readable content was found in fixture-runbook.md" — a false statement about a file that had 4 chunks.
resolvedDefects.evidence: Observed once at 19:50 after a brain restart. A POST reindex immediately restored 9 files / 18 chunks. NOT REPRODUCED on the next restart, where the index survived intact with all 9 counts present, so the restart itself is NOT established as the cause.
resolvedDefects.rootCause: indexService.sync() sets nextVersion = record.version + 1 on EVERY sync, including a no-op. commitSync() then persists only CHANGED chunks at that new version, so unchanged chunks keep their OLD index_version. A no-op sync therefore commits a version that holds ZERO chunks on disk while memory still holds the complete index. Approval points at that version. On the next restart loadVersion(approvedVersion) returns nothing and the index restores EMPTY while still reporting approved and searchable.
resolvedDefects.status: RESOLVED 2026-08-27 — option A shipped and proven in production.
resolvedDefects.effort: MEDIUM — the honest-state guard is EASY; the root cause is MEDIUM.
resolvedDefects.regressionTest: Wanted: an approved index that reports zero chunks must answer "index unavailable, reindex needed", never "no readable content was found in <file>". Approved+empty is contradictory state and must fail loudly.
resolvedDefects.reproduction: Occurrence 2 on 2026-08-27 immediately after the brain-release activation restart. Identical signature: state "approved", searchable true, stats files=0 chunks=0, empty chunkCounts — and the live product told the user "No readable content was found in fixture-notes.txt" about a real 2-chunk file. A POST reindex restored 10 files / 23 chunks and the same question then answered correctly (MT-PLAT-7731) with attribution.
resolvedDefects.triggerEvidence: BOTH occurrences followed a brain restart. It is NOT every restart: one intermediate restart left the index intact with all 9 counts present, so restart is a trigger but not a sufficient condition. That pattern fits a startup/lazy-restore race — status answers "approved" from the persisted record before the scoped chunk restore has populated the in-memory index — but the race has NOT been proven and must not be assumed.
resolvedDefects.userImpact: HIGH and silent. It does not error; it states a confident falsehood about the users own file, which is worse than an outage because nothing signals that a retry would work.
resolvedDefects.wantedFix: Approved + zero chunks is CONTRADICTORY state and must fail loudly: answer "index unavailable, reindex needed", never "no readable content was found in <file>". That guard is correct regardless of the underlying cause, so it can land before the race is proven.
resolvedDefects.proof: Instrumented and reproduced ON DEMAND, no waiting for a race. Before restart: loaded 23, recorded 0 — the approved version demonstrably held no chunks on disk. Restarted the brain: loaded 0, files 0, still "approved"/"searchable". Reindexed: loaded 23, recorded 23, because syncing from an EMPTY in-memory index marks every file changed and rewrites all chunks at the new version. That also explains why a reindex always appeared to "fix" it, and why only SOME restarts triggered it — it depends entirely on whether the last sync before the restart was a no-op.
resolvedDefects.guardLimitation: 🚨 The shipped guard does NOT catch this. It fires on recorded > 0 with loaded == 0, and here recorded is legitimately 0 because the version really does hold no chunks. The guard is still correct for what it covers and the honest-refusal plumbing is live and useful, but it must not be described as fixing this defect. It is what EXPOSED it.
fixOptions: A. Carry unchanged chunks forward to the new version on commit (re-stamp index_version for files that were not deleted). Correct under the existing snapshot model, but writes many rows.
B. Do not bump the version when nothing changed. Minimal, but needs care when only deletions occurred.
C. Make restore fall back to the newest version that actually holds chunks. Least invasive but leaves the incomplete version on disk as a trap for every other reader.
resolvedDefects.ownerDecisionNeeded: The version model comment in ragRepo.ts is explicit that an index legitimately holds the same chunk at two versions and that rewriting an older version destroys it. Choosing between A, B and C changes that contract, so it should not be decided unilaterally.
resolvedDefects.currentProductionState: HEALTHY as of 2026-08-27 03:2x — recorded 23 equals loaded 23, so a restart now restores correctly. The bug re-arms the next time a no-op sync commits.
resolvedDefects.resolution: Every committed index version is now a complete, independently loadable snapshot. The PostgreSQL writer carries untouched files forward inside the committing transaction; the superseded version is derived arithmetically as version-1, never read from the mutable workspace_indexes pointer.
resolvedDefects.verification: Gate 1 — full PostgreSQL suite 1958/1958, ZERO skips (Docker restored, so no test was silently absent). Gate 2 — all 8 carry-forward cases passed BY NAME, including MATRIX 8, the atomicity hard-stop: a rolled-back commit leaves no rows at the new version and no recorded count. Gate 3 — production proof on the live service: 23 chunks, no-op sync, new version still RECORDS 23 (this is the exact condition that used to record 0), Brain restarted, loaded == recorded == 23, and a grounded question answered VIOLET-ANCHOR-19 with correct attribution WITHOUT a reindex.

resolvedDefects.title: Image follow-through / conversational intent
resolvedDefects.reportedBy: Bonex, observed in a live session 2026-08-27 (screenshots kept as acceptance evidence). NOT independently reproduced by me yet.
resolvedDefects.symptom: With an image already active in the conversation and already successfully analysed, the follow-up "can you regenerate it?" failed to resolve against that image and asked the user to provide the content again.
resolvedDefects.acceptanceRule: When an image is active in the conversation, follow-up references — "it", "this", "same one", "remake it", "regenerate it", "make something similar" — MUST resolve against that image unless the user clearly refers to something else.
resolvedDefects.testMustVerify: 🚨 The resolved image actually REACHES the generation/editing routing layer. Proving the UI still displays the image is not proof; it is the same class of error as reading a rendered tile instead of the trace.
resolvedDefects.status: FIXED and live-proven 2026-08-27 (activeimg-61825461), one acceptance item pending.
resolvedDefects.rootCause: TWO causes, and the second was invisible until the first was fixed. (1) "regenerate it" had no intent of its own: it matched the UNDERSTAND patterns, so the turn went to the vision path and the model described the picture to someone asking for a new one. Eight of nine natural phrasings behaved that way. (2) The conversation's active image set only ever held UPLOADS — setConversationImages was never called with what a turn GENERATED — so after MigraPilot drew something there was no image for "it" to refer to.
resolvedDefects.fix: A `regenerate` intent, checked before transform and understand because it overlaps both and loses to either. Executability decided by PROVENANCE: a generated image carries the prompt that made it and is re-run; an upload cannot be reproduced and is refused plainly. And a generated picture now becomes the conversation's active image.
resolvedDefects.liveProof: Before: "regenerate it" answered "Sure! Please provide the text or content you'd like me to regenerate" — the reported sentence, reproduced verbatim. After: it produces the image, with no text. An uploaded photo refuses honestly and offers the alternative that works. Survives a hard reload: "make it again" executed on a reloaded conversation.
resolvedDefects.pending: Ordinary image UNDERSTANDING regression check is blocked by gpu-contention-starves-chat (GPU 23922MiB/100%, no Ollama models loaded, ComfyUI mid-render). Proven NOT to be a regression from this slice: the prompt classifies as `understand` on the unchanged path and wantsRegeneration is false, so the new code is never entered.

resolvedDefects.title: Regeneration promise vs execution truthfulness
resolvedDefects.symptom: MigraPilot answered "Sure! Please provide the content you'd like me to regenerate…", and then when given the image, described it again instead of regenerating or refusing honestly.
resolvedDefects.invariant: NEVER claim an image will be regenerated unless the request is actually being routed to an available image-generation capability.
resolvedDefects.requiredFlow: existing image + "remake/regenerate/something similar" -> recognise CREATION intent using the source image as reference -> if reference-based generation is supported, execute it and produce a new Media Library artifact WITH source provenance. If it is not supported: give a truthful capability refusal, do NOT describe the picture as though that satisfied the request, and do NOT say "Sure, I'll regenerate it".

withdrawnFindings.title: Generated image appears only after a reload
withdrawnFindings.symptom: A glyph turn streams route -> stage -> image -> done and the artifact is created, stored and linked to the assistant message, but the chat UI shows an EMPTY assistant message until the page is reloaded. On reload the image is there.
withdrawnFindings.evidence: Server side is fully proven: the Brain emits a 23,799-byte PNG frame, the consumer emits image {ref} with no error, GET /api/images/<ref> returns 200 image/png, and the Media Library grew 10 -> 12 for two NEW letters. Waited 112s during the live turn with no DOM image; the same artifact rendered immediately after refresh.
withdrawnFindings.whyItMatters: It presents exactly like a total failure. This is what made "Generate an image of the letter B" look like a classification bug for hours — the work succeeded every time and the user was shown nothing.
withdrawnFindings.status: DISPROVEN / CLOSED 2026-08-27 — retained in drift-control history only.
withdrawnFindings.withdrawal: I captured the "before" set of rendered images AFTER submitting the turn. The glyph path takes ~170ms, so the image was already in the DOM and was counted as part of the baseline — "no new image" was an artefact of the probe, not the product. Re-run with the baseline captured BEFORE submitting: the image renders live, visible at 1024x1024.
withdrawnFindings.verifiedInstead: All eight acceptance points pass live: frame arrives, message updates immediately, image renders BEFORE reload, same ref persists after reload, artifact present in the Media Library, a DUPLICATE content-addressed ref still renders immediately, text-only turns unaffected, and zero empty paragraphs on an image-only answer.
withdrawnFindings.probeDiscipline: For fast deterministic paths, capture the baseline BEFORE triggering the action. And never use artifact-count growth as evidence when content addressing can legitimately deduplicate identical output.

attachmentProcessingArchitecture_2026_08.status: PROVEN_LIVE 2026-08-30 — documents AND images. The image half found TWO real defects live; both fixed and deployed in consumer release imgrefusal-08300925.
attachmentProcessingArchitecture_2026_08.scope: Bonex reopened attachments after production screenshots: transport is fixed, processing limits are not.
attachmentProcessingArchitecture_2026_08.🚨 empiricalFinding_bonexPdfNeedsOcr: liv_kreyol_AI-Training.pdf (36 MB, 245 pages) has NO TEXT LAYER — probed on VM111, pages 122/123/124 each yield 0 characters. It is the scanned Kreyol book (HC-S009, 245 pages, the same source PASS 2 OCR'd). So the new text-layer fast path does NOT apply to it: the probe correctly routes it to the existing OCR pipeline. Expect roughly 1.5-2 hours for 245 pages at the PASS 2 measured rate (~24 s/page), not seconds. This is a real capability where there was none — the file used to be skipped outright — but it is SLOW for this document, and that must not be described as if it were instant.
attachmentProcessingArchitecture_2026_08.dragDropDefectFound: onDrop sent EVERY dropped file to uploadImage with no classification, so a dragged PDF was pushed at the image endpoint while the identical PDF chosen through the paperclip attached correctly. onPaste only looked for clipboard image MIME types, so a copied PDF pasted in did nothing at all — no attachment, no refusal, no explanation. Picker, drop and paste now share one `intake` that classifies from bytes via classifyAttachment. A local ACCEPTED_IMAGE_TYPES list was deleted; it claimed to be the shared definition but only paste consulted it.

largeDocumentIngestion.design: No new dependency. poppler 24.02.0 was already installed and already relied on by the scanned pipeline. `pdftotext -f N -l N` extracts ONE page per subprocess, so peak Brain memory is a page rather than a document, and a malformed PDF cannot take the process down with it — it dies in poppler's address space.
largeDocumentIngestion.routing: The runner probes the document and chooses: a real text layer takes the new textLayerPdfJob (seconds, order taken from the file); no text layer keeps the existing rasterise+OCR+reconstruct pipeline (minutes, order recovered from evidence). The probe samples from the MIDDLE, not page 1 — a scanned book's first page is often a near-empty cover and would misroute the whole document. If the probe was too optimistic the job falls back to OCR rather than failing.
largeDocumentIngestion.unblocked: index/route.ts no longer does `if (file.tooLargeToProcess) continue`. That single line was why an oversized PDF became a dead stored object: the 25 MB ceiling protects the SYNCHRONOUS parser and was never a claim the document is unreadable.
largeDocumentIngestion.🚨 syncCeilingUnchanged: MAX_EXTRACT_BYTES / DEFAULT_MAX_INDEX_FILE_BYTES stay at 25 MB. The synchronous in-request parser was NOT widened — that was the explicit instruction and the whole point. Large documents are read out of the request, a page at a time.

attachmentProcessingArchitecture_2026_08.stateModel: The state machine already existed for OCR escalation (stored/processing/ready/too_large_to_process/no_text_layer/ocr_failed, with a `polling` flag and a contributesToAnswers() gate). It is now also used for large documents. New: the index route returns `processing[]`, outcomeOfIndex checks it BEFORE the chunk count (a document being read has no chunks, which was being explained as 'no readable content'), and the chip has a `processing` state that polls /api/files until the server says polling:false. Terminal state is taken from `readable`, never from the job merely having stopped. `groundable` still requires `ready`, so a processing document cannot ground an answer.
attachmentProcessingArchitecture_2026_08.notBusyOnPurpose: `processing` is excluded from `busy`. Busy holds the composer, and a background read takes minutes — locking someone out of their chat because a large PDF is indexing would trade one broken capability for a worse one. The chip states the real state instead.
attachmentProcessingArchitecture_2026_08.testsCorrectedNotWeakened: Four tests asserted the old source shape. 'picker, paste and drop all go through the same upload' PASSED while onDrop was broken — it only checked each handler eventually reached uploadImage, which was never the property worth protecting. It now asserts all three go through intake and that the image uploader has exactly ONE call site.

remaining.nonPdfLargeFiles: A >25 MB CSV/TXT still has no background reader and is still honestly reported as too_large_to_process. DELIBERATELY out of scope: Bonex scoped this to 'supported PDFs above 25 MB'. Closing it means teaching the chunker to accept a stream, which is a deeper change to the indexing pipeline than attachments should carry.
remaining.deploy: BOTH consumer and brain-service changed. Both need releasing before live proof.

attachmentProcessingArchitecture_2026_08.🚨 sharpMustNeverBeAdded: I previously proposed adding sharp for image resizing. That would have BROKEN PRODUCTION and the codebase already documents why: sharp's prebuilt Linux binaries require the x86-64-v2 microarchitecture, the production VM reports a 'Common KVM processor' with neither SSE4.2 nor AVX2, so its own guard refuses the native binding and falls through to a WebAssembly build that dies on missing Wasm SIMD — an error with no `code`, which crashes sharp's error formatter and takes the importing module down. It already broke a turn once. downscale.ts is deliberately pure JS (jpeg-js + pngjs) so the path the tests exercise is the path production runs. DO NOT REINTRODUCE IT.
attachmentProcessingArchitecture_2026_08.🚨 correctionIssued: I reported 'no downscaling exists anywhere'. That was WRONG — I searched only apps/brain-service/src/engine/vision/ and generalised. Downscaling already existed in the consumer at server/files/downscale.ts, with the original preserved, a cache, and measured numbers (4032x3024 photo: 28.4s to first token full-size, 1.94s at 1024px). The architecture Bonex asked for was already built for JPEG and PNG; the real gap was narrower.

imageIntake.ceiling: MAX_IMAGE_BYTES 8 MB -> 25 MB. The old limit refused ordinary phone photos.
imageIntake.whySafe: Only because the derivative already existed: downscaleForModel caps what vision receives at 1024px on the longest edge, so a 25 MB original costs the GPU no more than a small one. The library keeps the original bytes, the content hash stays valid, and the transcript shows the user's real picture.
imageIntake.🚨 realGapFound: GIF and WebP have NO pure-JS decoder, so they get no derivative and reach the model at FULL resolution. Vision cost is set by pixels, not bytes — so raising the byte ceiling alone would have handed the model a 6000px WebP and spent half a minute of somebody's turn on it, which is exactly what Bonex said not to do. Unresizable formats are therefore bounded by DIMENSION (MAX_UNRESIZABLE_EDGE = 2048, chosen from the same measurements: 1568px answered in 3.56s). The refusal names the way out — re-save as PNG or JPEG — because 'too large' alone would leave someone cropping a picture when re-exporting would have worked.
imageIntake.noDrift: RESIZABLE_FOR_MODEL lives in images.ts and downscale.ts imports it, so intake's decision to APPLY the pixel rule and downscale's decision to PRODUCE a derivative cannot disagree. A test asserts decodesForModel() matches the set for all four formats.

🚨 criticalDefectFoundByTracing.what: fsFileSource's walk skipped any file over the extraction ceiling BEFORE looking for an OCR sidecar. Once oversized PDFs started going to the background reader, that ordering meant a 36 MB scanned book would be OCR'd for ~2 hours, write a perfectly good sidecar, then be skipped by the walk — zero chunks indexed — and the runner's own honesty check would report 'the pages were read but nothing could be indexed from them'.
🚨 criticalDefectFoundByTracing.severity: This would have made the ENTIRE large-document feature silently fail after two hours of the user's time. Every component was correct in isolation; only the ORDER of two checks was wrong, which is why no existing test could see it. Found by tracing the full path from job -> writeOcrSidecar -> indexService.sync -> walk, not by a failing test.
🚨 criticalDefectFoundByTracing.fix: The sidecar is checked FIRST for PDFs; the size ceiling then applies to every path that reads SOURCE bytes. The ceiling protects this walk from loading a large file into memory, and a sidecar is a different, already-bounded artifact whose existence proves the source was read out-of-band.
🚨 criticalDefectFoundByTracing.regressionTestVerified: test/largePdfSidecarIndexing.test.ts. PROVEN to catch the defect: with the old ordering temporarily restored the suite failed 1/2071 on exactly that test, and passed again once reverted. A test that passes both before and after would have proven nothing.

hashBasedReuse.design: uploaded file -> SHA-256 (streamed) -> artifact registry lookup -> reuse, else ingest.
hashBasedReuse.askedFirst: Before probing or rendering. The cheapest work is the work not done.
hashBasedReuse.identity: The DIGEST, never the filename. A name is a label a user can change, and attaching one book's text to another book's bytes is far worse than redoing the OCR. A registry entry whose recorded digest disagrees with its own filename is REFUSED.
hashBasedReuse.🚨 trustNeverPromoted: Registered pages stay machine_extracted / certified:false. The importer REFUSES any record claiming certified:true. Reused pages carry confidence 0.9 rather than 1.0 — a text-layer PDF's order is stated by the file, this order is inherited from an extraction whose own confidence varied page by page. Every page's evidence string reads 'reused from HC-S009, engine tesseract, langs hat+fra, 300dpi, pass 2, certified false'.
hashBasedReuse.failsOpen: Any registry failure falls through to real ingestion. Reuse is an optimisation.

2_alteredBytes.verdict: DEFECT FOUND - the test did not do what it looked like it was doing.
2_alteredBytes.observed: Uploaded an altered copy under the SAME filename. It showed 'Ready' instantly with no OCR. The reuse decision was never reached: the file replaced the original on disk while its readiness row and index entry survived. Deleting it first and re-uploading the altered bytes ALSO went Ready in ~40s with zero OCR.
2_alteredBytes.rootCause: OCR sidecars are keyed by FILENAME, and a filename is not an identity. Neither delete path removed the sidecar: deleteFile removes only the PDF, documentForget removes only the readiness row. So the walk found the previous document's sidecar and indexed ITS text under the new file - ready, searchable, and citable, for a document that was gone.
2_alteredBytes.severity: Provenance corruption, and PRE-EXISTING - but my own change (sidecar checked before the size ceiling) made it reachable for large files that were previously skipped outright.
2_alteredBytes.fix: writeOcrSidecar records the source SHA-256; fsFileSource refuses a sidecar whose digest does not match the bytes in front of it; delete now removes the sidecar. A sidecar with NO digest is still trusted so shipping this does not discard hours of completed OCR - the exception closes itself as sidecars are rewritten. Three regression tests, NEGATIVE-CHECKED: with the check neutered the suite fails on exactly that test.

🚨 measurementErrorCorrected.what: I reported 'the Brain had consumed 6 SECONDS of CPU across 493 seconds of uptime' as evidence that HC-S009 ran no OCR. That measurement was WRONG: `ps -o time=` reports CPU for the node process only, and tesseract runs as a CHILD process whose CPU it does not count. The correct measure is the cgroup (systemctl show -p CPUUsageNSec), which counts children - and which showed 268s for a job I had just measured as '23s' the wrong way.
🚨 measurementErrorCorrected.doesTheConclusionSurvive: YES, on other evidence. HC-S009 reached ready in ~20 SECONDS OF WALL CLOCK for a 245-page scan; OCR of that book takes over an hour however CPU is measured. pgrep -x tesseract and pdftoppm were both 0, and the answer carried PASS 2 OCR artefacts. The conclusion holds; one of the four pieces of evidence I cited for it did not.
🚨 measurementErrorCorrected.pattern: Second measurement artifact in this session, after a pgrep watcher that matched its own command line. Both were caught by re-deriving the number rather than trusting it. Prefer cgroup CPU over per-process CPU whenever child processes do the work.

staleWindowTightened.reason: Bonex's directive after the live test confirmed the misleading state. Fifteen minutes of 'Reading text - page 10 of 24' for a dead process is worse than an honest failure, because the user waits on it.
staleWindowTightened.alreadyHeartbeatBased: No change needed there - staleness was ALREADY measured from `updatedAt` (last write), not from job start, and every stage transition upserts it. The scanned job writes BEFORE each page, so the heartbeat is every 15-24s at the measured OCR rate: two minutes allows five to eight missed heartbeats.
staleWindowTightened.🚨 whyAggressiveIsSafe: The clock is NOT what protects a running job - `activeJobs` is. A job owned by this process returns 'leave' before the idle check is reached, whatever the stage and however long it has been quiet. That matters for `indexing`, the one stage that is a single long operation rather than a per-page loop. The threshold governs only rows whose owning process is gone. Pinned by a test asserting an owned job is left alone after an hour idle.
