chatRepairPass_rootCause_2026_08_29.status: PROVEN_LIVE 2026-08-30. Both defects fixed, deployed and verified through the real chat UI.
chatRepairPass_rootCause_2026_08_29.🚨 headline: MigraPilot Chat has NO multi-turn conversational memory through the Brain, and never has. The consumer never sends `conversationId` on a chat turn, so the Brain cannot scope anything to a conversation - not history, not grounding. Every turn reaches the model standalone: prompt + groundingFiles + imageAttachments, and nothing else.

codeEvidence.consumer: The ChatTurn operation type in src/server/brain/operations.ts has NO conversationId field. Its fields are prompt, conversationSummary, stream, groundingMode, attachments, imageAttachments, groundingFiles. The stream route HAS the conversationId - it uses it to persist messages - and simply never forwards it.
codeEvidence.conversationSummary: The only history-carrying field is `conversationSummary`, read from the REQUEST BODY, i.e. supplied by the browser. Nothing in the UI ever sets it. So it is always undefined.
codeEvidence.brain: apps/brain-service/src/engine/aiRoutes.ts:115 declares conversationId?: string. Line 536 `memoryStore && body.conversationId ? getConversation(...) : undefined`. Line 551 buildContext({ conversationId: conv.id, retrieve: true }). The entire durable-memory machinery is built, correct, and unreachable because the field never arrives.

chatRepairPass_rootCause_2026_08_29.🚨 productionProof_reloadWasIncidental: Bonex framed this as post-reload context divergence. The reload is NOT the boundary. Reproduced in a BRAND-NEW chat with NO attachments and NO reload: turn 1 'Remember this code for later: ZULU-4417' -> 'Acknowledged: ZULU-4417.'; turn 2 'What was the code I just gave you?' -> MigraPilot invented a Python add_numbers(a, b) function. Same failure shape as the PyPDF2 hallucination he saw. The real boundary is ANY follow-up that depends on a previous turn rather than on a document. His inference from the evidence he had was reasonable; the cause is broader.
chatRepairPass_rootCause_2026_08_29.sharedRootCause_PROVEN: YES - #1 and #2 share one. Because the conversation's identity never reaches the Brain, the ONLY cross-turn context that exists is `groundingFiles`. That set is deliberately additive-forever in the stream route: `const requestedGrounding = [...new Set([...storedGrounding, ...attachedNow])]` with the comment 'Attaching adds to the thread's set; it never silently replaces what is there.' So files became the sole carrier of continuity, and every file ever attached stays an equally active retrieval target for every later turn. #2 is not an independent bug; it is what the system does INSTEAD of having conversation memory.
chatRepairPass_rootCause_2026_08_29.whyThisMattersForTheFix: Fixing #2 alone - scoping grounding to the current turn - would REMOVE the only continuity the product has and make follow-ups worse. The two must be fixed together: send conversationId so real history works, THEN narrow grounding to current-turn attachments plus explicitly referenced ones.
chatRepairPass_rootCause_2026_08_29.notYetInvestigated: Defects #3 (large digital PDF), #4 (DOCX), #5 (arithmetic), #6 (GPU readiness), #7 (vision text), #8 (blank conversation).

defect1_conversationMemory.rootCause: The consumer's ChatTurn operation type had no `conversationId` field, so it was never sent, so the Brain's `body.conversationId` was always undefined - and its entire durable-memory path is gated on that one value. Chat had NO cross-turn memory.
defect1_conversationMemory.fix: conversationId declared on the operation type, declared again on the chatTurnStream seam (this file's own comments warn twice that excess properties are not checked through a spread, so a field declared at one end and not the other is silently dropped), included in the request body, and forwarded from the stream route which had always known it.
defect1_conversationMemory.contextIsBounded: Bonex's guardrail was already satisfied by the Brain's existing contextBuilder and needed no change: 3000-token budget, `limit: 20` recent COMPLETE messages, a compressed summary for older history, workspace memories, and `omittedForBudget` diagnostics for traceability. Durable memory means reconstructable and retrievable, not append-forever.

defect2_groundingIsolation.rootCause: `[...new Set([...storedGrounding, ...attachedNow])]` - every file ever attached stayed an equally active retrieval target forever. Deliberate, and a direct consequence of defect 1: with no history, documents were the ONLY carrier of continuity.
defect2_groundingIsolation.fix: New pure module server/files/turnGrounding.ts. Current-turn attachments are active; historical files NAMED in the prompt are reactivated; with neither, the conversation's set stands so a one-document thread's bare 'summarise it' still works. The thread still PERSISTS every file - narrowing what is active is not forgetting. The route now sends turnGrounding.active as the retrieval boundary, and traces reason/active/withheld.
defect2_groundingIsolation.whyOrderMattered: Fixing this alone would have removed the only continuity the product had. It is safe only because history now flows.

defect3_largeDigitalPdf.rootCause: The text-layer probe averaged 3 clustered pages against a 120-char bar. A PDF is large because it embeds images, so exactly the documents most likely to be big are the ones where a title page, a full-page image and one dense page average below the bar. The 40 MB digital PDF was therefore sent to OCR, which recovered nothing from a document whose text was sitting right there, and the user was told it was unreadable.
defect3_largeDigitalPdf.fix: The probe samples 8 pages SPREAD across the document (front matter is unrepresentative in both directions) and accepts EITHER signal: mean >= 120 chars, or any single page >= 200 chars, which is a paragraph rather than a scanner artefact. Plus a safety net in the runner: if OCR recovers nothing, the text layer is tried before reporting failure, because 'OCR found nothing' and 'there is nothing to find' are different claims. Costs nothing on a genuine scan.
defect3_largeDigitalPdf.notFixedByForcingOcr: Explicitly per instruction - a scanned PDF still probes false and still takes OCR, pinned by test.
defect3_largeDigitalPdf.caveat: Diagnosed by mechanism, NOT against Bonex's actual 03_large_digital_40mb.pdf - that file is in his library and not readable from the host. The fix must be proven against HIS file in the live sweep.

governingRule: ⭐ Manage the roadmap by CAPABILITY COVERAGE, not by backend subsystem. For every user need ask: can the user do it now; is it exposed in the product; is it real end to end; does it persist across reload; does it fail honestly; is it useful without knowing the backend. Infrastructure work only gets priority when it directly blocks a capability the user should have in hand. ⭐ AND: no capability is PROVEN_LIVE until tested with the owner's OWN real file/content/use case. Fixtures qualify an implementation; they never close a capability.

capabilityCoverage._method: Audited against the CONSUMER product surface (chat.migrateck.com), not backends. A backend that exists but is not reachable from the product counts as MISSING, because the user cannot use it.

LIVE.chat / reasoning: Proven repeatedly today, including under GPU recovery.
LIVE.files and documents: TXT, MD, CSV, JSON, source code, PDF text-layer, scanned PDF via OCR, and DOCX — with attribution, history, detach, deletion, readiness states.
LIVE.images (understanding): Vision answers from the image; attachment history, per-conversation isolation, unreadable-image handling.
LIVE.image generation: Generation, persistence, glyph rendering, conversational reference and truthful regeneration.
LIVE.audio / voice: Input (dictate/transcribe) AND output (Read aloud, Kokoro primary with Piper fallback, engine names never exposed). Both self-hosted, both CPU, neither touching the GPU.

PARTIAL.spreadsheets / data analysis: CSV reads, grounds and attributes correctly, but quantitative reasoning is a known open defect (wrong maximum, mistranscribed numbers). Reading works; ANALYSIS does not.
PARTIAL.exports / sharing: Account-data export exists. No conversation export or sharing.

productStandard._authority: Bonex, 2026-08-27. Governing. Supersedes any narrower rule it conflicts with.
productStandard.premise: MigraPilot is built on limited local infrastructure today but must be designed and implemented as if it will compete with major AI systems at production scale.
productStandard.currentStageRule: The workstation and its RTX 3090 are a DEVELOPMENT/PROOF environment, not the deployment target. Slower performance caused strictly by limited local hardware is ACCEPTABLE. Incomplete, fake, fragile, mediocre or shortcut implementations are NOT. Never lower capability quality because the machine is small — record slowness as a hardware/performance constraint instead.
everyCapabilityMust: work end to end through the real user product
be complete within its defined scope
use real backend logic — no placeholders, no UI-only behaviour
be live-tested in the actual product, not accepted on unit/integration tests alone
be tested against Bonex's own real files/content/use cases before PROVEN_LIVE
preserve provenance, ownership, isolation and canonical state
be architected to scale onto larger servers/GPU clusters later WITHOUT redesigning the capability
productStandard.technologySelection: Prefer the best self-hosted, open-source, free-commercial or already-owned option, qualified on actual measured quality and licensing. Custom-build orchestration, UX, persistence, routing, safety, quality control and integration where that produces a stronger owned product. No recurring paid dependencies unless there is no viable alternative and the value justifies it.
productStandard.roadmapDiscipline: Capabilities in the user's hands, never backend subsystems. Ask constantly: "What can the user do now that they could not do before?" If a batch cannot answer that, verify it directly unblocks a user-facing capability — otherwise it is drift.
productStandard.acceptanceAuthority: Live product behaviour. Tests are necessary but never sufficient. Ask: "If this feature were completely absent, what observable behaviour would be different?" — then prove that difference through the real product.
productStandard.target: A system demonstrable to investors, partners, buyers or customers as a complete, ownable, scalable AI platform. Build the product we intend to sell, not what today's workstation runs comfortably.

closed.3 stop generation: LIVE — proven end to end against the production Brain (qwen3:8b) on 2026-09-03

evidence_stop.control: The send button BECOMES Stop while a turn streams — one slot, two states, so a second turn can no longer be fired into a conversation already receiving one. Enter obeys the same rule.
evidence_stop.mechanism: The browser aborts the request (network shows ERR_ABORTED). The route's cancel() returns the Brain generator, whose finally releases the upstream reader. Server trace for the stopped turn: outcome="cancelled", model qwen3:8b.
evidence_stop.🚨 loadBearingMechanism: The REQUEST SIGNAL, not the response cancel. Proven by writing the test the other way first: cancelling only the response stream calls cancel(), which awaits frames.return() — and the generator is suspended on an upstream read a still-generating model never settles, so the return queues behind it and NOTHING unwinds. request.signal is what rejects that read. Removing `signal: request.signal` from the route makes the regression test hang.
evidence_stop.partialAnswer: KEPT on screen and labelled "You stopped this answer. It was not finished, so it was not saved." Neutral, not amber: a stop is not a fault. A turn stopped before any output keeps nothing and says so.
evidence_stop.honesty: Verified by reload: the question survives, the stopped partial does not — exactly what the label promises.
evidence_stop.🚨 defectFoundAndFixed: My own first implementation SENT A MESSAGE when Stop was clicked. Reproduced deterministically in a real browser: two requests for one click. type="button" was already correct and did not save it — onStop aborts, the rejection lands on the microtask checkpoint at the end of the click handler, React clears pending and re-renders, and because both branches render a <button> in the same position React PATCHED THE CLICKED NODE to type="submit" before the browser ran the click default action. Fixed with preventDefault() plus distinct React keys so the node is replaced, not retyped. Both defences mutation-tested.
evidence_stop.tests: +28: src/state/stopGeneration.test.ts (27 — registry behaviour, the stopped-vs-dropped distinction, the outcome rule, and wiring guards) and one route test, "STOP: a browser that hangs up mid-answer cuts the Brain off". Every guard proven by reintroducing its defect.
evidence_stop.gate: typecheck 0 · 737/737 tests pass (from 709) · next build green · client-bundle scan PASS · 13/13 live browser checks pass.
evidence_stop.notDone: The partial answer is not persisted, so a stopped turn still vanishes on reload. That is the stream route's existing rule (only a completed turn is stored), stated honestly rather than changed. Persisting stopped partials is a separate decision.

evidence_askAgain.🚨 theConstraint: THE CONVERSATION STORE IS APPEND-ONLY, and that decides the feature. Measured, not assumed: the Brain exposes create / append message / list messages / delete-whole-conversation and NOTHING else — no remove-one-message, no truncate-after, no parent or branch column anywhere in memoryRoutes or the Postgres repos. So the regenerate and edit of other chat products (the old answer disappears behind a 2-of-2 arrow) are capabilities MigraPilot does not have.
evidence_askAgain.whyNotBuiltAnyway: It would produce a transcript that rearranges itself on reload: one answer in the browser, two in the durable record, and no way for the reader to tell which they were looking at. evidence_askAgain.shipped: "Try again" on the last answer (asks the same question again, carrying the same attachments, images and Migra family) and "Edit and ask again" on any question (loads it back into the composer, focused, cursor at the end). evidence_askAgain.offeredOnlyOnTheLastAnswer: A repeat appends to the BOTTOM of the thread, so repeating an older question would drop its answer underneath a conversation that has moved past it. shipped.files: apps/brain-service/src/engine/tools/idempotency.ts (pure state machine), idempotencyStore.ts (port + in-memory), sqliteIdempotency.ts (durable), test/idempotency.test.ts
shipped.uniqueKey: PRIMARY KEY (idempotency_key, actor, scope). NOT the key alone — two tenants would collide. NOT the whole identity — a changed input hash would INSERT A SECOND ROW instead of colliding, so the reuse would succeed as a new operation. Tool and input hash are columns compared on read; the collision has to happen for the refusal to be possible.
shipped.atomicClaim: One INSERT; the database decides who wins. Read-then-write loses the double-click race: both callers dispatch and the operation happens twice with an audit trail saying it happened once. Proven by a concurrent-claim test.
shipped.identityBeforeState: A committed record whose key was reused for different input reports the REUSE, never the stored result — otherwise a caller receives a stranger's outcome for their own operation.
shipped.outcomeUnknown: Not a retry state, and there is no flag to make it one. reattempt() refuses from it by name; only reconcile() moves it, and only when the caller has found out what happened.
shipped.freshAttempt: failed_before_dispatch → pending is deliberately NOT a transition. reattempt() mints a new attempt with an incremented counter, so the second try is visible rather than erasing the first.
shipped.durability: Every invariant runs against BOTH the in-memory and SQLite backings, and durability is proven by closing the database and reopening it. An invariant proven only in memory says nothing about the property this exists to provide.
shipped.mutationTested: All four named classes fail targeted tests: dropping uniqueness, allowing a changed hash, letting outcome_unknown retry, letting a committed record dispatch.
shipped.notYetWired: 🚨 NO capability consumes this yet. Wiring the first non-idempotent tool is a separate slice with its own acceptance.

2_durableIdempotency.design: A PLATFORM PRIMITIVE, not a rename special case. One authority, no per-tool copies. Keyed on canonical normalized operation identity: idempotencyKey + toolId + actor + scope + normalizedInputHash → pending | committed | failed_before_dispatch | outcome_unknown, with a durable result / reconciliation record.

releaseModel._authority: Bonex, 2026-09-08. Named explicitly so the two models are not conflated.
releaseModel.why: The consumer deploy rebuilds from source, and Next mints a random BUILD_ID per build, so no prequalification build can BE the artifact later activated.
releaseModel.whatMakesItValid: One uninterrupted run must build, stage, boot-test, identity-assert, cut over, and independently verify the running process, with NO rebuild between boot qualification and activation.
releaseModel.verifiedHow: Read deploy-consumer.sh step order: npm run verify (step 3, the only build) -> stamp+read BUILD_ID from that .next (4) -> tar THAT .next to the release dir (4b) -> boot-test that directory (5-7) -> ln -sfn to the same directory (8) -> assert running process (10). No build command exists between step 4 and step 8.
releaseModel.invariant: If HEAD changes after the final handoff, cutover approval is VOID and the release must be re-qualified from the new HEAD. This prevents single-pass from degrading into qualify-one-commit-deploy-another.
releaseModel.rehearsalMeaning: A MIGRAPILOT_QUALIFY_ONLY run is evidence about the PIPELINE, not the identity of the future production artifact.

item1.title: Brain buildId is not a complete release identity
item1.evidence: FAILED chat-platform-rc-0907 and QUALIFIED chat-platform-rc-0907b share buildId sha256:90fd92a97e630bbe53a3d9c720c48a45998fb252.
item1.why: BUILD_ID digests dist/ only. The rc-0907 failure lived in node_modules (a stale workspace package), which the digest does not cover. The fix was entirely in docs/migrapilot/*.sh, which do not compile into Brain dist, so the compiled bytes are genuinely identical.
item1.consequence: Identity assertion by buildId alone would have PASSED the release that could not boot. Only the workspace staging-parity gate distinguishes them.
item1.remedy: Report a manifest/digest over the whole RUNTIME CLOSURE as the deployable artifact identity: Brain dist + runtime workspace-package bytes + package metadata/export maps + the staged runtime dependency manifest.

item2.title: Next buildId is a RUN identity, not a source/content identity
item2.evidence: Two rehearsals over IDENTICAL consumer source (only docs/migrapilot changed between 909ea46f and 94c6c20c) produced ILw_YGfCaw10U3fRcAi4Q and z3Xkf4jduHFJlR-zk5fWe. A content-derived id would have been unchanged.
item2.why: apps/migrapilot-consumer/next.config.* declares no generateBuildId override, so Next emits a random per-build id.
item2.consequence: No prequalification build can be the artifact later activated. This is what makes single-pass qualification-and-activation the correct DESCRIPTION of the current chain rather than a workaround.
item2.remedy: A content-derived generateBuildId, so a consumer artifact identity is reproducible from source.

p0ColdStart.rootCause: The Brain AUTHORS user-facing prose in the stage event's detail field and the consumer displayed it verbatim. The earlier cold-start work fixed the indicator's SHAPE — no avatar, bubble, timestamp or controls — and that held; nothing ever asked what the WORDS were. It was never the image route: image understanding runs the text path, the only lane that emits loading_model.
p0ColdStart.canonicalFix: The stream boundary forwards the stage CODE and drops the prose, so a Brain sentence never reaches the browser bundle. state/turnStatus.ts maps codes to product-owned copy; an unmapped stage renders bare dots rather than an invented description. Deliberately NOT a denylist — a filter passes the next sentence nobody thought to ban.
p0ColdStart.tradeRecorded: The image queue's 'Waiting behind N job(s)' count existed only inside the prose, so it is gone. Recovering it means the Brain emitting the count as a FIELD. Follow-up, not smuggled in.
p0ColdStart.mutations: map the stage back to the Brain sentence -> 3 tests fail; forward detail at the boundary again -> boundary test fails.

p0AnonymousProjectState.rootCause: An anonymous visitor is a REAL principal, so the routes' !resolved guard never fired. The call reached the Brain, which correctly found no grant for an anonymous scope and refused, and the route rendered its only sentence for a refusal — revoked access. The system refused too much; it never granted too much, and authorization is untouched.
p0AnonymousProjectState.canonicalFix: server/projects/projectPrincipal.ts holds one capability rule (canHoldProjects, an allowlist on session) and one refusal (sign-in, 401). All three project routes consult it. sign-in also became its own UI state with a sign-in action — it previously shared the retry branch and rendered a sentence with nothing to click.
p0AnonymousProjectState.mutations: let anonymous hold projects -> capability test fails; restore request-read-access -> refusal test fails; a route stops consulting the rule -> wiring test fails.

p0SpreadsheetEnumeration.rootCause: detectOperation had no enumeration branch, so 'List the four Revenue values, exactly as they appear' matched nothing, produced no evidence, and fell through to the document-search refusal — which then advised asking about a column, the thing that had just been done.
p0SpreadsheetEnumeration.canonicalFix: list is an operation in the shared substrate. It has its own column chooser because identifier semantics are about ARITHMETIC: summing postcodes is meaningless, reading them back is an ordinary question. It reproduces stored text rather than parsed numbers, names blanks, and states the bound when a column exceeds 50 rows. Checked LAST so an explicit aggregation still wins.
p0SpreadsheetEnumeration.honestFinding: THREE mutations escaped on the first pass and the TESTS were wrong, not the code. The leading-zero guard was vacuous — ZipCode parses as an identifier, so the mutant fell back to identical output. The truncation guard matched a directive line instead of the fact it meant to guard. Blank handling was unasserted. Strengthening the third exposed a real fabrication in the NEW code: 'n/a' printed as '(blank)', because kind==='blank' covers both an empty cell and a written non-value. Emptiness is now decided by the text.
p0SpreadsheetEnumeration.preserved: Genuine free-form document search still produces no evidence and still refuses — enumeration was widened, not the capability claim.

p1FilesLibraryReuse.gap: Both paperclip rows opened the OS picker, which cannot see a file already on the server. Reuse meant finding the original on disk and re-sending bytes.
p1FilesLibraryReuse.fix: A third row lists the caller's own library. No upload, copy or duplicate index; the file is addressed by its stored name and settled through the SAME readiness step as an upload, extracted so the paths cannot drift. Dispatch cannot distinguish them.
p1FilesLibraryReuse.notIncluded: Images. They live in a separate content-addressed store, so the work order's 'if supported by the same canonical file store' condition does not hold. Recorded, not faked.
p1FilesLibraryReuse.collateral: A test asserting the menu had exactly two gated rows failed on a correctly-gated third. The count was a bad statement of a right property; it now counts gates against rows and rejects an ungated addition.

p1WebProjectCreation.verdict: BLOCKED — deliberately not built. No shortcut taken.
whatWasFound: There is NO create/register route in the project lane at all — only list, get binding, connect, disconnect.

The sole registration path is POST /api/ai/workspaces, which takes a CALLER-SUPPLIED root. Correct for the extension, where the root is a folder on the user's own machine; a server file-read hazard on the web, where it names a path on VM111's disk. Any signed-in user could register /etc and read it through the inspect pipeline.
workspaceGrantSource.ts already records this limit in its own header: closing it is a change to REGISTRATION, not to the grant source.

A governed per-user root DOES exist — userDirectory() = UPLOAD_ROOT/sha256(scope.owner), session-derived, hashed so no identifier can produce a path separator, mode 0700 — and Brain and consumer share a host in production, so it is technically reachable.
whyNotBuiltAnyway: It would institutionalise the consumer-to-Brain shared-disk coupling that this file's own csvGroundingTopology entry flags as 'a deployment constraint to solve — not something to institutionalise'.
It requires a NEW Brain route registering a workspace with a server-resolved root — new authority surface, not a wiring change.
It requires deciding what a 'project' MEANS for a Web user. Rooting one at the user's document area makes the word mean something different in Web than in the extension. That is a product decision.
Registering authorized project roots is a CONTROL-PLANE concern under the locked rule: MigraPilot ships PRODUCT ONLY; admin goes to the Migra control panel.
p1WebProjectCreation.recommendation: Introduce an operator-governed catalog of authorized project roots in the Migra control plane. Web users connect to what the catalog has granted them; the browser never names a path, and the Brain resolves the root from the catalog row. This fits the existing governance split, closes the caller-supplied-root hazard for every client at once, and does not require the Web app and the Brain to share a disk.
p1WebProjectCreation.currentUserState: Truthful and unchanged: 'No projects are available to connect yet.' A dead end, but it asserts nothing false and does not send a Web user to VS Code.

evidenceQualityLesson._authority: Bonex, 2026-09-08, asked that this be preserved as a standing lesson.
evidenceQualityLesson.lesson: A mutation test must prove the assertion is sensitive to the actual SEMANTIC CONDITION, not merely that it executes the path.
howItWasLearnedHere: Three mutations escaped the new spreadsheet suite and the TESTS were at fault, not the code.
The leading-zero guard was vacuous: ZipCode parses as an identifier, so swapping raw text for the parsed value produced identical output and the mutant survived.
The truncation guard matched a DIRECTIVE line that happened to contain the same words as the FACT it meant to guard, so deleting the fact still passed.
Strengthening the third exposed a real fabrication in the newly written code: 'n/a' was printed as '(blank)', because kind==='blank' covers both an empty cell and a written non-value.

The live cold-start harness had the same disease: it DETECTED cold starts by the forbidden string and watched that string on the progress surface throughout without objecting. That is how a green harness coexisted with the production failure.

suiteInclusionIsTheAuthority._authority: Bonex, 2026-09-08, asked that this be kept in the engineering record.
suiteInclusionIsTheAuthority.lesson: A direct test invocation is not suite-inclusion evidence. The suite gate is the authority.
suiteInclusionIsTheAuthority.whatHappened: 17 search tests were written under src/engine/search/. The Brain's runner globs dist/test/**, so the suite never loaded them. They compiled and passed when invoked directly, and a commit message claimed 'Brain 2501/2501' when the real count was 2484 and those assertions were guarding nothing.
suiteInclusionIsTheAuthority.whyItMatters: This is the same shape as every other false-green in this record: a check that exists, appears to pass, and is not actually connected to the thing it claims to guard. Reading the number from a direct run rather than from the gate is what made the claim wrong.
suiteInclusionIsTheAuthority.caughtBy: test/suiteCoverage.test.ts, which compares what exists in source against what the runner will load. The repo already knew this mistake was possible before it was made.
suiteInclusionIsTheAuthority.rule: Report counts only from the suite command. Never from a targeted invocation.

fixturesCanPassForTheWrongReason._authority: Bonex, 2026-09-08: these are evidence-quality failures, not implementation mistakes.
fixturesCanPassForTheWrongReason.lesson: A fixture that passes does not show the factor under test is doing anything. Isolate it: hold every other component equal and give the factor the disadvantage, so only it can move the outcome.
instances: Dedup reordered results when rank and array position disagreed — real providers return in rank order, so it would have hidden until one did not.
The `web` catalog row had no handler: unclickable while unavailable, a dead control the moment a provider is configured.
A readiness test asserted a set of four literals it declared itself — worthless against any implementation.
Ranking fixtures for directness and syndication passed while those factors were disabled entirely.

emptyOutputIsNotEvidence._authority: Bonex, 2026-09-08, asked that this be preserved permanently.
emptyOutputIsNotEvidence.rule: A suite gate only counts if the gate actually COMPLETED and PRINTED the result. Empty output is not evidence.
emptyOutputIsNotEvidence.whatHappened: A commit claimed 'Brain 2694/2694, from the suite gate' while `tsc -b` was failing, so the suite never ran. The verification grep matched nothing, and the number was stated anyway. This was the SECOND count-reporting failure in one session; the first read a count from a direct invocation the suite had never loaded.
emptyOutputIsNotEvidence.whyTheFirstLessonWasInsufficient: 'The suite gate is the authority' is true and does not help if you do not read what it says. Silence was treated as success.
emptyOutputIsNotEvidence.mechanicalFix: docs/migrapilot/suite-gate.sh runs the suite and REFUSES to report unless a final count was printed, the counts reconcile (pass+fail+skipped == tests), no test failed, and the runner exited zero. Verified against a broken build and a failing test.
emptyOutputIsNotEvidence.preCommitFinding: 🚨 The pre-commit hook's `npx tsc --noEmit || true` would NOT have caught this. Measured: with a deliberate type error in a brain-service test, the ROOT tsc reports 0 matches while the app's own `tsc -b` reports it. The hook typechecks a different project, so removing `|| true` is a real improvement in principle and would not have prevented this incident.
emptyOutputIsNotEvidence.preCommitRecommendation: Removing `|| true` is safe TODAY (root tsc is currently clean at 0 errors) but is a repo-wide policy change: a future unrelated app breaking would block every commit across the monorepo. Recorded as backlog rather than changed unilaterally, per Bonex's instruction. The protection that actually works for this failure is running suite-gate.sh before quoting a count.

migraSearchProgress._authority: Bonex work order chunk 2, 2026-09-08. SearXNG is the first retrieval backend, never the product contract.
migraSearchProgress.status: READY FOR PROVIDER INTEGRATION — every code path built and mutation-tested; waiting on hardware

completed.fetchBoundary: parse -> scheme -> resolve -> screen EVERY address -> connect PINNED -> verify the peer -> redirect re-enters the loop -> bounded body. The pin is what makes screening enforceable: resolve-then-hand-the-URL-to-a-client is time-of-check-to-time-of-use, and a hostile zone answers the first query publicly and the second with 169.254.169.254. A transport that cannot report its peer is refused, because absent proof is not proof. 7 mutations, all caught.
completed.extraction: Page text, headings, lists, tables, content hash. Absent stays absent: no date becomes today, no title becomes the URL slug, no lang becomes a guess. Publication dates come from an allowlist because <meta> is an open namespace and `expires`/`revised` are date-shaped non-dates. A table without <th> gets no invented headers. Hand-rolled rather than a DOM library: this parses attacker-controlled input inside the Brain's process.
completed.evidenceModel: Six typed evidence objects. A citation may only reference retrieved evidence, and the realistic violation is not an invented URL — it is a claim written from a fetched PAGE with a citation assembled from the search RESULT that led to it. Untraceable citations are REJECTED, not downgraded: an unverifiable citation converts 'I could not find this' into false confidence. Sufficiency is derived, never set.
completed.readiness: The registry gained an optional cheap synchronous readiness probe and an engine-owned unavailableReason. A missing GRANT deliberately gets no user-facing reason — 'you lack terminal.exec' is scaffolding. Four failure states held apart: not_configured, provider_unavailable, provider_timeout, no_results. Only the last is a claim about the world.
completed.registration: migra.search registered with the web.search grant HELD and no provider. Reports 'Web search is not set up yet.' Omitting it until a backend exists would teach people the product cannot search — a worse untruth than saying it is not set up.
completed.composer: One catalog entry, four lines, naming a capability id. No composer change was needed, as the hub slice predicted. The composer does not know which backend answers a search, whether it is healthy, or that none exists.
completed.planner: Deterministic routing with reason codes. Default is NOT to search: being wrong that way costs freshness, being wrong the other way costs quota and an answer contaminated by a page the user never chose — and only the second is hard to notice. Attachments beat topical signals, because 'the LATEST figure in this spreadsheet' carries the strongest positive signal and is not a web question. An explicit request beats attachments. 5 mutations, all caught.
completed.ranking: Migra-owned reranking above provider order. No favourite-domain list: directness is DERIVED from the query, so an unknown vendor ranks correctly on the day they launch. Weights are chosen PER QUESTION — a fixed table let a 2019 page beat a week-old one on a query that said 'latest', because a table that cannot express 'the user asked for recency' makes provider rank the final authority wherever it matters. Every profile is asserted to sum to one. Extraction quality is a MULTIPLIER, not a weighted term: an unreadable page cannot support a citation, so its other virtues are irrelevant rather than outweighed.
completed.canonicalOriginality: Canonical-link evidence resolves the recorded provider-rank guess: a third-ranked original now outranks a first-ranked syndication when copies name it. A cross-domain canonical is accepted ONLY as SELF-DEMOTION, never as a claim over another page — otherwise any site could declare itself canonical for a competitor's article and inherit its standing. Provider-rank fallback retained and now says 'by provider rank' in its reason so a trace shows which basis was used.
completed.searxngAdapter: The only file that knows SearXNG exists — its parameters, JSON, engine names, error strings and host all stop there. Written and mutation-tested against recorded payloads with NO backend, which is also the state it must keep working in when the backend is down. No exception becomes 'nothing found': a 429 is unavailability (SearXNG returns it when upstreams rate-limit), and a 200 with an unrecognised shape is a broken backend. Only an empty results array yields no_results. providerRank is the row position, not SearXNG's score, whose scale is not stable across queries or versions.

escapedMutations: UI hardcoding the provider reason. Swapping Search's catalog source from `registry` to a `local` readiness carrying 'SearXNG is not running' passed the entire suite. The authority boundary could be INVERTED while every user-visible test stayed green. Guards are permanent, per Bonex.

Ranking: removing DIRECTNESS and removing the SYNDICATION PENALTY both left all sixteen ranking tests green. The fixtures were passing for the wrong reasons — the docs case carried by intent-path matching, the syndication case by the original happening to hold the best provider rank. Isolating fixtures added that hold every other component equal and give the factor under test the worse provider rank, so it must overturn something. Both now fail.
defectsFoundInOwnWork: Dedup moved a group to its later member's position when rank and array position disagreed — a reorder from a stage whose contract is that it only removes. Real providers return in rank order so it would have hidden until one did not.
The `web` catalog row had no handler: unclickable while unavailable, a dead control the moment a provider is configured. Guard added comparing catalog ids to the handler map.
A readiness test asserted a set of four literals it declared itself — worthless against any implementation. Replaced with one that drives the real code down each path.

searchCoreCapacityBlocker._authority: Measured on the Proxmox node, 2026-09-08, before creating anything. Bonex authorised VM creation IF legitimate Proxmox access existed; it does, and the host cannot take the VM.
searchCoreCapacityBlocker.verdict: BLOCKED — migra-search-core NOT created. The node has no memory to give it.
searchCoreCapacityBlocker.proxmoxAccess: Confirmed available: root on the node, qm and pvesh present. The blocker is CAPACITY, not authority.

measured.node: single node — pvesh get /nodes returns one entry, so there is no cluster member to place it on
measured.allocatedToGuests: ~81.5 GB (VMs 62.6 GB + LXC limits 18.9 GB) on a 64 GB host — 27% oversubscribed
measured.actualVmRss: 59,117 MB across 12 running VMs. Guests are USING their allocations; this is not idle over-allocation.
measured.disk: 96 GB free — disk is NOT the constraint

searchCoreCapacityBlocker.whyNotProceed: Adding a VM means taking memory from a running guest or pushing the host deeper into swap. Either risks the production services on this node — including the VM running the Brain and Consumer deployed 2026-09-08. That crosses the standing rule: never break production for acceptance work.
searchCoreCapacityBlocker.secondaryFinding: INDEPENDENT OF SEARCH: this host is already precarious at 96% memory and 92% swap, with customer-facing services co-resident alongside production MigraPilot. Worth attention regardless of whether search ever ships here.
optionsForBonex: Add RAM to the node. 64 -> 128 GB is the cleanest fix and also relieves the pre-existing pressure.
A second Proxmox node for platform services. Larger change; matches the 'search is a platform service' framing.
Reclaim from a guest — but RSS shows they are using what they hold, so this means genuinely shrinking a workload, not trimming slack.

An LXC instead of a VM. Far lower overhead (no guest kernel), SearXNG plausibly fits in ~512MB-1GB. Still needs memory this host does not comfortably have, and departs from the 'dedicated VM' instruction.
Defer. The architecture already handles this honestly — migra.search stays registered-but-unavailable with 'Web search is not set up yet.' Nothing is broken by waiting.
searchCoreCapacityBlocker.phasesBlocked: 1 through 7, and 9 through 13. All depend on the host existing.
searchCoreCapacityBlocker.phaseCompletedAnyway: Phase 8 (canonical-link originality) needed no provider and is done.

decision.chosen: OPTION 2 — provision a SECOND Proxmox node for shared platform services.
decision.target: 128 GB RAM minimum, with CPU and NVMe headroom, so Search + Maps + later platform services do not immediately recreate the same ceiling.
decision.hostsWhat: migra-search-core first, then migra-local-core, then other shared non-customer-facing platform services.
decision.currentNode: Keep as-is until a deliberate rebalance. Recorded separately as an operational capacity risk.

rejectedAndWhy.addRamToExistingNode: Helps, but leaves one failure domain and customer workloads competing with platform services.
rejectedAndWhy.lxcInsteadOfVm: The dedicated VM was chosen for isolation and a clean service boundary. Switching to LXC because the host is saturated solves the symptom by weakening the architecture.
rejectedAndWhy.shrinkAGuest: Not without a workload-by-workload capacity study. RSS evidence shows real consumption.

decision.blockedOn: PROCUREMENT. Provisioning a second physical node means ordering hardware, which the agent cannot do. This is Bonex's purchase decision.

ballooningInvestigated._note: Checked as a possible way to avoid buying hardware. It does NOT hold, and the check is recorded so nobody re-derives it.
ballooningInvestigated.whatLookedPromising: Guest `free -m` reported ~27 GB 'available' across six VMs, which looked like reclaimable slack.
ballooningInvestigated.whyItIsNot: The balloon device reports the guests' real free memory: app-core 556MB free of 16004, migrapilot-app-core 316MB of 5925, migrapanel-core 328MB of 7941. The 'available' figure is almost entirely PAGE CACHE. Reclaiming it via ballooning would force guests to drop their caches, trading host memory for guest I/O.
ballooningInvestigated.worseStill: MigraPanel-Core reports mem_swapped_out=3.3GB — that guest is already swapping INTERNALLY, so it is memory-pressured, not idle.
ballooningInvestigated.separateFinding: `balloon` is UNSET on every guest except one. Worth configuring on its own merits for elasticity, but it is not a way to fit a search VM on this node.

migraEmailProgress._authority: Bonex work order, 2026-09-08. Gmail is the first provider, never the product contract.
migraEmailProgress.status: COMMITTED — NOT DEPLOYED. Production serves 0f494d27 (chat-platform-rc-0908, built 2026-09-08); local HEAD is 3c204aa8. The Gmail/chat work is 65 brain + 11 consumer + 3 shared-types commits ahead of it. No staging environment exists. Nothing deployed.

suiteGate.brain: 3050/3050 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped (was 3016; +25 Gmail transport tests, 3 mutations caught)

built: Contract: connection/authorization/health as THREE axes, read and send as separate capabilities, bodyComplete on every message.
Send governance: propose -> approve -> RECHECK AUTHORIZATION -> durable claim -> dispatch. Uncertainty settles to outcome_unknown and is terminal.
Recipients: ambiguity REFUSED, never resolved by recency — 'usually right' is what trains a user to stop reading the recipient.
Read path: only a provider that answered with an empty list reaches no_results; threads sorted chronologically; membership never inferred from subject.
Evidence: bodyComplete ENFORCED — completeness is derived, not trusted, and one snippet makes a whole summary partial.
Attachment bridge: parses nothing, hands off the same canonical file object an upload produces, policy INJECTED so limits have one authority, provenance survives.
Intent routing: an ACTION over the mailbox is required; a bare mention is not an intent.
Draft: local composition only; a forward does NOT inherit the thread; reply-all excludes the sender.
Telemetry: shapes not content; the event type has no field that could carry an address or subject.
Capability + hub: migra.email registered, read-only, reporting 'Email is not set up yet.'

Gmail adapter TRANSPORT: search/readMessage/readThread/listAttachments/readAttachment call the real Gmail API. Injected fetch + our own timeout ceiling. createDraft/send remain unimplemented ON PURPOSE — the refusal is the absence of code, not a flag, and no mutating verb or path appears in the file (asserted against the source).
defectsFoundInOwnWork: 🚨 THE READ SLICE WAS NEVER CONNECTED TO GMAIL. Every layer above the adapter was built, mutation-tested and reported COMPLETE while GmailProvider had ZERO HTTP: every operation returned unconfigured() unconditionally, ignoring even a valid access token. With a real consented connection, sealed tokens and readiness reporting available:true, every search returned not_configured. 3016 tests passed over it, because the whole read path was tested against FAKE providers. A fake proves the shape of a contract; it cannot prove anyone implemented it. The status file even recorded "adapter shell" — and the slice was still called complete.

🚨 CREDENTIAL LEAK: JSON.stringify(GmailProvider) serialised the access token, because TypeScript's `private` is compile-time only and the field stayed an enumerable own property. Any logger or error report carrying the provider would have carried the token. Now an ES #private field with an explicit toJSON.
Address parsing split '"Okafor, James" <j@x>' inside the quoted display name, producing a recipient called 'James' and losing the real one.

🚨 ROUTING: 'My inbox is a disaster, anyway — what is the capital of Peru?' routed into a mailbox SEARCH. A bare state word was sufficient, so a noun being present was enough to open private correspondence to answer a geography question.
'Make this email shorter' fell through to an incidental mention because the rewrite pattern required adjacency.

overnightAudit2026_09_12.🚨 P0_capabilityAnswersBypassTheRegistry: The assistant misdescribes its own capabilities IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. It offers web search and audio transcription it does not have, and denies file reading, image understanding and conversation memory that it demonstrably does. 10 verbatim examples in the report. The capability registry holds the exact answer including each unavailableReason — the consumer already fetches it to draw the action hub, which IS truthful. This is the capability-owned-answer principle violated on a new surface: a model regenerating facts the system knows exactly. NOT FIXED — answering capability questions from the registry is a feature, not a narrow defect.
overnightAudit2026_09_12.🚨 P0_fixed_deepTierWentOffDevice: tier=deep routed to gpt-oss:120b-cloud — 384 BYTES on disk advertising 116.8B parameters, an Ollama Cloud manifest. A staging turn sent 335 input tokens to it while the engine reported provider=local, under a provider declared dataLocality on-device at cost 0. It wins the deep tier outright because that tier scores +0.05 per billion parameters. Contradicted three standing rules at once. FIXED 58e14894: labelled and excluded unless MIGRAPILOT_ALLOW_REMOTE_MODELS=1; deep tier keeps deepseek-r1:32b on the machine.
overnightAudit2026_09_12.🚨 P0_fixed_stubProviderLookedHealthy: A Brain with NO inference reported status ok with all four providers reachable. StubProvider.isAvailable() returned true unconditionally and the probe short-circuited stubs to reachable with one advertised model; only gpuCapacity told the truth. FIXED 58e14894 with a kind: live|stub on every health line, a new stub status, and 8 regression tests. The stub still WORKS — only its claim changed.
overnightAudit2026_09_12.routingTruth: The env profiles DO NOT drive chat. /api/ai/chat uses ModelRegistry + capabilityRouter (capability-driven, explicitly not env vars); MIGRAPILOT_*_MODEL feeds the older per-profile registry that chat never consults. At balanced with no hints the SIZE TIE-BREAK decides: llama3.1:8b 0.84 vs qwen2.5-coder:14b 0.72. Consequences: reasoning models are unreachable from the consumer (it never sets needsReasoning nor requests deep, so migra-logic can never be reached); isCodingIntent is a 7-word regex missing javascript/sql/git/postgres; tier=fast picks the SMALLEST model, landing a greeting on qwen2.5-coder:1.5b with a non-instruction-tuned BASE model ranked second.
overnightAudit2026_09_12.P1_noModelAttributionAnywhere: Brain returns model/provider/tier/routing.reason. Consumer /api/chat keeps model+provider and DROPS tier and routing. /api/chat/stream emits no model at all. conversation_messages HAS model_id and provider_id and the consumer appendMessage operation does not carry them: 82 assistant rows, 0 with a model. The durable record of every staging answer cannot say what produced it.
overnightAudit2026_09_12.P1_fixed_tooLargeReportedAsEmpty: A 28.6 MB file of plain repeated ASCII stored fine and then answered "No readable content was found in huge.txt. Attach a file with text in it." Above the 25 MB extract ceiling it is never parsed, so the index holds the same zero chunks an empty file would. FIXED 50e2bcec — names the limit, 5 regression tests.
overnightAudit2026_09_12.P1_unreproducibleUngroundedDenial: PRESERVED, NOT RETRIED AWAY. In the first batch after the initial upload, four attachment questions answered "I do not see an attached file" from the MODEL with no error event. Did not reproduce across 8 later attempts with identical prompts and files. The refusal paths do work (document_not_attached and insufficient_evidence both fire, including immediately after a fresh upload). The dangerous shape is that the failure was an ungrounded model denial rather than a refusal.
overnightAudit2026_09_12.attachmentsProven: txt/csv/json/pdf: uploaded -> stored -> indexed -> UNDERSTOOD, with citations (note.txt:1-2, sales.csv:3, report.pdf page 1) and exact values (3310.25). Images stop at STORED. Audio and .doc are refused with actionable messages.
overnightAudit2026_09_12.visionGapIsGovernance: 4 vision models INSTALLED; ingestion, storage and multimodal routing all work. state=no_qualified_model. Staging governance is UNSIGNED so no approval can even be recorded here. Production has a signed approval and reports migra-vision available. Requirement: a signing key on staging, then one signed approval. No model download needed.
overnightAudit2026_09_12.webSearch: NOT CONFIGURED by design — MigraSearch holds null and says so. Dependency: a SearchProvider implementation plus self-hosted SearXNG (migra-search-core). No paid service, no credential.
overnightAudit2026_09_12.gmailBlocker: 🚨 THE BLOCKER IS THE ORIGIN. oauthConfig refuses a non-HTTPS public origin when NODE_ENV=production, and staging runs production deliberately. http://127.0.0.1:3200 CANNOT be the Gmail origin. Needs staging-chat.migrateck.com (DNS+TLS), then ONE redirect URI in Google Cloud: https://staging-chat.migrateck.com/api/account/mail/callback. Token sealing is AES-GCM with associated data binding ciphertext to scope+provider+account+purpose, so a grafted token fails to open.
overnightAudit2026_09_12.securityBoundaries: Tenant isolation enforced on owner AND workspace (wrong owner 404, wrong workspace 404, unscoped sees nothing) plus database FORCE RLS — the app role sees 0 of 96 conversations. Staging role CONNECT to production = false. Production DB 200 MB unchanged. No secrets in logs (variable NAMES only). Env files 600.
overnightAudit2026_09_12.backupReality: A cluster-wide pg_dumpall runs on db-core daily at 02:30 UTC as postgres, 7-day retention, root-only; last run succeeded. It covers migrapilot_brain_stage — BUT the staging DB was created at ~06:30 UTC today, AFTER today's run, so the first backup containing it is tomorrow's. Two ad-hoc defects found: an app-role pg_dump FAILS LOUDLY under FORCE RLS (the good outcome) and CT101 ships a v15 client against a 16.15 server. Restore rehearsal NOT performed: CREATE DATABASE is permitted by the guard but DROP DATABASE is not, and leaving an undeletable copy of conversation data on the production DB server is worse than not rehearsing.

rollbackProof_2026_09_13.🚨 thereWasNoRollbackCommand: There was no rollback COMMAND for MigraPilot — only a line the deploy scripts PRINTED: ln -sfn $PREVIOUS $ROOT/current && systemctl restart. It repoints `current` and never touches `previous`. Survivable while previous did not exist; once it became a durable recorded pointer the line became ACTIVELY WRONG — run it and both pointers name the same release, so there is no way back from the way back, and retention sees rollback == active and demotes the real spare. A rollback that leaves the pointers incoherent is not a rollback; it is a symlink swap that happens to work once.
rollbackProof_2026_09_13.theMechanism: docs/migrapilot/rollback.sh --target <t> --app <consumer|brain> [--to <r>] [--apply]. Plans by default. Checks the destination AND THE RELEASE BEING LEFT with the shared completeness predicate (the latter becomes the new `previous`). Swaps both pointers TOGETHER, `previous` FIRST — a death between the writes leaves current=A previous=A, visibly wrong and harmless because nothing moved; the other order moves the service and erases the way back. Asks the RUNNING PROCESS what it serves, retries, and never translates "could not reach it" into "serving the wrong thing". Refuses to infer a target from directory age. IT IS ITS OWN INVERSE, which is what makes a two-way proof one command run twice.
